Recent Fills SHALL render the last 20 entries of recent_fills reversed to newest-first, with Time as HH:MM:SSZ from the ISO fill timestamp, Symbol, a signed Qty at 6 decimals colored green when qty_delta is greater than or equal to zero and red only when it is strictly negative, Price at 2 decimals and Fee at 4 decimals, showing "no fills" when the list is empty. Every symbol and violation string SHALL be HTML-escaped before interpolation (&, <, >, ", '), and any unparseable timestamp SHALL render as --. Before the first render lands, the static markup SHALL show its own placeholders ("no data" in the Positions table body and the weights box, "none" for violations, "no fills" for fills).

docs.title: Scenario: Fills tape is capped client-side
docs.text:
• WHEN the state document carries more than 20 recent fills
  • THEN only the last 20 are shown, newest first, while the endpoint still returns the trader's full capped tape

docs.title: Scenario: Empty panels
docs.text:
• WHEN positions, weights, violations or fills are empty in the state document
  • THEN each panel shows its own placeholder text rather than an empty table body

docs.title: Requirement: Equity curve canvas
docs.text: The system SHALL draw the (deposit-adjusted) equity_curve on a plain 2D canvas with no charting library: 180 CSS pixels tall, as wide as its own client width (falling back to the parent panel's width), scaled by devicePixelRatio so it stays sharp on retina displays, and redrawn on every render pass - which means a window resize is picked up by the next 1 Hz re-render rather than by a resize handler. An empty curve SHALL draw the text "no equity data yet" instead of axes. Otherwise the chart SHALL use a fixed padding of 60 left, 12 right, 12 top and 22 bottom, map x linearly across the epoch-millisecond range and y across the value range (expanded by plus and minus 1 when every point is identical so a flat curve still has a scale, and with either span floored at 1), draw five horizontal gridlines at equal fractions of the y span with right-aligned y labels formatted with en-US grouping and no decimals, stroke the line green when the last value is greater than or equal to the first and red otherwise, and fill the area under the line with the same hue at 8 percent opacity.

docs.title: Scenario: No equity points yet
docs.text:
• WHEN the equity curve is empty
  • THEN the canvas shows "no equity data yet" instead of an empty axis frame

docs.title: Scenario: Flat curve
docs.text:
• WHEN every equity point has the same value
  • THEN the y range is widened by plus and minus 1 so the line renders instead of dividing by a zero span

docs.title: Requirement: Weight-history heatmap
docs.text: The system SHALL draw a "position tape" heatmap of the /api/weights history on its own canvas: one column per bar and one row per symbol. The tape SHALL therefore show the trader's TARGET weights, because weight_history entries are [epoch_ms, target_weights] and the trader stores only nonzero, non-NaN targets. It SHALL require at least two history entries; with fewer it SHALL hide the canvas, show "building weight history..." and clear the hover layout so hovering does nothing. Rows SHALL be selected by summing the absolute weight of each symbol across the window, dropping every symbol whose total is at or below 1e-4 (rotated-out tails), sorting the rest by that total descending and capping at 90 rows (HM_ROWS), then re-sorting the surviving rows by the most recent bar's weight so the biggest longs sit on top and the biggest shorts at the bottom; the panel title SHALL be rewritten to "Portfolio Weights - History" suffixed with the resulting row count as " names". The number of columns is bounded by the trader's weight_history_max (96 bars, about 48 hours of 30-minute bars), not by the page. Cell color SHALL diverge from teal rgb(38,208,160) for long through near-black rgb(16,22,31) at zero to red rgb(248,81,73) for short, normalized by the largest absolute weight among the DRAWN rows (floored at 1e-6) and lifted by a 0.68 gamma so small weights stay visible. Layout SHALL use a 70 pixel label gutter, 8 pixel right pad, 4 pixel top pad, 18 pixel bottom pad, 13 pixel rows, 1 pixel cell gaps and 2 pixel rounded corners, scaled by devicePixelRatio, so the canvas height grows with the row count. Row labels SHALL be the symbol with the first occurrence of USDT removed by a plain string replace (not an anchored suffix strip); up to 7 evenly spaced HH:MM UTC time labels SHALL run along the bottom. Hovering a cell SHALL show a floating tooltip, clamped to the viewport width, with the symbol, the bar time as HH:MMZ and the weight as a percentage with 2 decimals colored green or red - rendered with a plain toFixed, so negatives keep their minus sign but positives carry NO leading +. The tooltip SHALL be hidden when the pointer leaves the grid or the canvas. A window resize SHALL redraw the heatmap after a 150 ms debounce, and the heatmap SHALL otherwise be redrawn only by the /api/weights poller, not by the 1 Hz re-render.

docs.title: Scenario: Not enough history
docs.text:
• WHEN fewer than two bars of weight history exist
  • THEN the heatmap canvas is hidden and the panel shows "building weight history..."

docs.title: Scenario: Only the actively-held book is shown
docs.text:
• WHEN the window contains symbols whose total absolute weight is at or below 1e-4
  • THEN those rows are dropped, the remaining names are capped at 90 rows and ordered longs-first by the latest bar, and the title reports how many names are drawn

docs.title: Scenario: Cell hover
docs.text:
• WHEN the pointer rests on a heatmap cell
  • THEN a tooltip shows that symbol, the bar time in UTC and the weight as a colored percentage with no explicit plus sign on longs

docs.title: Requirement: Page layout
docs.text: The system SHALL lay the page out as a wrapper capped at 1280 pixels wide, a flex-wrapping status bar, then a two-column CSS grid that collapses to a single column at or below 860 pixels of viewport width. The Equity Curve, weight-history heatmap, Positions and Recent Fills panels SHALL span the full grid width, while Target vs Actual Weights and Risk Violations SHALL sit side by side in the two-column layout. The connection status line SHALL sit right-aligned at the bottom of the page. The palette SHALL be a dark theme with green for gains, red for losses and amber for warnings, and all numeric cells SHALL use the monospace class.

docs.title: Scenario: Narrow viewport
docs.text:
• WHEN the browser viewport is 860 pixels wide or less
  • THEN the panel grid collapses to one column and every panel spans it

docs.title: Requirement: Venue snapshot sidecar
docs.text: The system SHALL provide a separate venue-snapshot sidecar (dashboard/venue_snapshot.py, run as python -m alpha_engine.dashboard.venue_snapshot and documented to run under its own systemd service trading-venuesnap with EnvironmentFile=secrets/binance.env; no unit file for it is checked into deploy/systemd/ and deploy/RUNBOOK.md never mentions it). At import it SHALL read VENUE_SNAP_SECONDS (default "15", parsed with int, so a non-numeric value raises ValueError at import), VENUE_SNAPSHOT_PATH (default /opt/trading/state/venue_snapshot.json) and the required BINANCE_API_KEY / BINANCE_API_SECRET (a missing key raises KeyError at import, so the process fails fast instead of polling unauthenticated). Every loop iteration it SHALL call the signed USD-M REST endpoint /fapi/v2/account and, when more than 60 seconds have passed since the last successful transfer refresh, re-page the whole /fapi/v1/income history with incomeType=TRANSFER; the base URL https://fapi.binance.com is hard-coded (mainnet only, no testnet switch). Each call SHALL append timestamp (epoch ms) and recvWindow=10000, sign the url-encoded query with HMAC-SHA256 over the secret, send the key in the X-MBX-APIKEY header, and time out after 10 seconds. Transfer history SHALL be paged in explicit 30-day [startTime, endTime) windows walking forward from the hard-coded account epoch 1783468800000 (2026-07-08 00:00 UTC) up to now + 60000, with limit=1000 per page and the cursor advanced to the last row's time plus 1 ms while a full page comes back, because the income endpoint honours explicit bounds while an open-ended query silently serves only recent history; consequently one further REST call is added for every extra 30 days elapsed since the epoch. Amounts SHALL be taken as float(row["income"]) with no asset filtering - the module documents that stable-asset amounts (USDT/USDC) are treated as $1 units, but it does not check the field. The result SHALL be written atomically (temp file created with mkstemp in the destination directory, then os.replace; the temp file is NOT unlinked if the write raises) as compact JSON {ts, equity, wallet, unrealized, transfers[[epoch_ms, amount], ...]} where ts is the writer's own epoch ms, equity is totalMarginBalance, wallet is totalWalletBalance and unrealized is totalUnrealizedProfit. The loop SHALL then sleep VENUE_SNAP_SECONDS, so the effective cadence is the interval plus request latency. Any exception in an iteration SHALL be printed as venue_snapshot: <error> on stdout (flushed, for the journal) and the loop SHALL continue, keeping the previously fetched transfers in memory and leaving the last snapshot file in place; because the write is the last statement in the try block, a transfer-fetch failure also skips that iteration's account-number write. The dashboard SHALL serve that file read-only from the state file's own directory as the hard-coded name <state-dir>/venue_snapshot.json and SHALL NOT read VENUE_SNAPSHOT_PATH itself, so in production the sidecar's output path and the state file must share a directory; the web-facing process never holds API keys. A snapshot file that exists but is not valid JSON SHALL propagate the parse error (HTTP 500) exactly as the state file does - only a missing file yields the no_snapshot marker. The dashboard SHALL expose no staleness signal for the snapshot, so a sidecar that has died keeps serving its last file with an old ts and the page shows those numbers as if they were live.

docs.title: Scenario: Snapshot refresh
docs.text:
• WHEN the poll interval elapses
  • THEN the sidecar overwrites the snapshot atomically with the fresh account numbers and the cached transfer history

docs.title: Scenario: Transfers are cached
docs.text:
• WHEN less than 60 seconds have passed since the last transfer fetch
  • THEN the sidecar reuses the in-memory transfer list and only refreshes the account numbers

docs.title: Scenario: Poll failure keeps loop alive
docs.text:
• WHEN a REST call fails
  • THEN the sidecar prints the failure and sleeps until the next poll instead of crashing, the previous snapshot file stays on disk, and no snapshot is written for that iteration

docs.title: Scenario: Missing credentials
docs.text:
• WHEN BINANCE_API_KEY or BINANCE_API_SECRET is not set
  • THEN importing the module raises KeyError and the sidecar never starts polling

docs.title: Requirement: Launch and deployment contract
docs.text: The system SHALL have no dashboard subcommand in the repo CLIs: the root main.py only exposes live-trade and nothing under tools/ starts a web server, so the only entry point is an ASGI server pointed at the module-level app, canonically uvicorn alpha_engine.dashboard.app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 with LIVE_STATE_PATH set. The shipped systemd unit (deploy/systemd/trading-dashboard.service) SHALL run exactly that command from /opt/trading/venv/bin/uvicorn as the unprivileged trader user with Type=simple, WorkingDirectory=/opt/trading/backend, Environment=LIVE_STATE_PATH=/opt/trading/state/live_state.json, EnvironmentFile=/opt/trading/secrets/dashboard.env for DASH_USER / DASH_PASS (whose example file ships DASH_USER=viewer and a placeholder password), After/Wants=network-online.target, Restart=on-failure with RestartSec=5, MemoryMax=512M, stdout/stderr to the journal, and WantedBy=multi-user.target. The app SHALL be bound to loopback only and fronted by Caddy (deploy/Caddyfile), which auto-provisions a Let's Encrypt certificate for kolyan.tech, adds a second basic_auth layer (user viewer, bcrypt hash placeholder REPLACE_WITH_BCRYPT_HASH that the operator must replace) in front of the app's own cookie auth, gzip-encodes responses via encode gzip, reverse-proxies to 127.0.0.1:8000, sets X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, and logs to /var/log/caddy/kolyan.tech.log. Provisioning SHALL be handled by deploy/install.sh, which installs Caddy and the Python venv and instructs the operator to copy deploy/systemd/*.service and deploy/Caddyfile into place; it installs no sidecar unit for venue_snapshot. The runtime dependencies SHALL be fastapi>=0.115 and uvicorn[standard]>=0.30 from the root requirements.txt. The app SHALL provide no rate limiting of its own.

docs.title: Scenario: Production start
docs.text:
• WHEN systemctl enable --now trading-dashboard is run on the deployed host
  • THEN uvicorn serves the app on 127.0.0.1:8000 reading /opt/trading/state/live_state.json, with app-level auth from dashboard.env and Caddy terminating TLS in front

docs.title: Scenario: No CLI launcher
docs.text:
• WHEN an operator looks for a python main.py dashboard style command
  • THEN none exists - the dashboard is started only by running an ASGI server against alpha_engine.dashboard.app:app

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines the historical bulk-download pipeline of binance_parser: the standalone tools/history.py CLI (download and funding subcommands), per-market file address resolution on the public data archive (data.binance.vision), batch download with checkpoint resume and SHA-256 verification, CSV-to-parquet conversion, and the funding-rate REST backfill.

docs.title: Requirement: History CLI contract
docs.text: The system SHALL expose a standalone tool at binance_parser/tools/history.py that boots its own sys.path so it works both as python tools/history.py ... and python -m tools.history ..., owning only the CLI surface while delegating logic to the download service. It SHALL offer a download subcommand with --market (spot|usdm|both, default spot), --group (all|major, default all), --symbols (explicit list that overrides the group), --types (defaults to klines, aggTrades and bookTicker), --months (default 12), --intervals (defaults to 1s and 1m; applied to klines only), --workers (default 8), --dry-run, and -y/--yes. It SHALL offer a funding subcommand with --group (all|major, default major), --symbols, --months, and --dry-run. Symbols passed explicitly SHALL be checked against the static pair list with a warning for unknown ones; without --symbols the group resolves to the major pair list (or all pairs for all).

docs.title: Scenario: Default download run
docs.text:
• WHEN python tools/history.py download is run with no flags
  • THEN it resolves the spot market, the all group (all pairs), the default types (klines, aggTrades, bookTicker), the default kline intervals (1s, 1m), and 12 months of lookback, then prepares download entries

docs.title: Scenario: Dry-run estimate
docs.text:
• WHEN download is run with --dry-run
  • THEN it prints the estimated file count and exits without any network I/O

docs.title: Scenario: Large run confirmation
docs.text:
• WHEN a download resolves to more than 1000 files and -y/--yes was not passed
  • THEN it prompts for confirmation via input() before starting

docs.title: Scenario: Unknown symbol warning
docs.text:
• WHEN --symbols contains a symbol outside the static pair list
  • THEN the tool prints a warning naming the unknown symbols

docs.title: Requirement: Download address resolution
docs.text: The system SHALL build one download entry per (market, symbol, data type, period) via the spec builder. Past months SHALL resolve to a single monthly ZIP; the current month SHALL resolve to one daily ZIP per day up to and including today. Klines SHALL be multiplied by the configured intervals; all other data types SHALL be single un-intervaled entries. Address bases SHALL come from the venue map: spot https://data.binance.vision/data/spot, usdm https://data.binance.vision/data/futures/um. Interval filenames SHALL omit the data type (BTCUSDT-1m-2024-03.zip); un-intervaled filenames SHALL be SYM-{data_type}-{period}.zip. Every ZIP SHALL have a sibling .CHECKSUM address.

docs.title: Scenario: Monthly archive file
docs.text:
• WHEN a spot klines entry targets a past month for BTCUSDT with interval 1m
  • THEN the address is https://data.binance.vision/data/spot/monthly/klines/BTCUSDT/1m/BTCUSDT-1m-2024-03.zip with sibling BTCUSDT-1m-2024-03.zip.CHECKSUM

docs.title: Scenario: Daily archive file
docs.text:
• WHEN a usdm aggTrades entry targets a day in the current month
  • THEN the address is https://data.binance.vision/data/futures/um/daily/aggTrades/BTCUSDT/BTCUSDT-aggTrades-2024-03-01.zip

docs.title: Scenario: Kline intervals only
docs.text:
• WHEN a non-klines data type (aggTrades, bookTicker, trades) entry is built
  • THEN it carries no interval and its filename has no interval segment

docs.title: Requirement: Download, verification, and conversion loop
docs.text: The system SHALL download entries concurrently with a worker pool, skipping any entry whose output parquet already exists. Each ZIP SHALL be fetched together with its sibling .CHECKSUM file and verified with SHA-256. A 404 for the ZIP SHALL return no path (the file is not on the archive); the batch loop SHALL count it as a failed entry (there is no separate not-found counter). A checksum fetch that raises (connection error or timeout) SHALL log a warning and proceed WITHOUT verification (a documented trade-off); a non-200 checksum response (e.g. a 404 on the .CHECKSUM itself) SHALL be treated silently as unavailable and verification SHALL be skipped without a log. A checksum mismatch SHALL retry the entry, and after three failed attempts SHALL log it as failed. The CSV SHALL be parsed from the first .csv inside the ZIP with fixed column names per data type (12 for klines including the ignore column; 7 for aggTrades; 7 for trades; 7 for bookTicker), cast to the anchored parquet schema, and written atomically; schema-less fallback writing SHALL be unreachable because all four data types have schemas. Columns absent from the anchored schema (such as ignore) SHALL be dropped.

docs.title: Scenario: Existing output skipped
docs.text:
• WHEN the output parquet path already exists
  • THEN the entry is resolved without any network I/O and counted as done (only entries already recorded in the checkpoint are counted as skipped on a resumed run)

docs.title: Scenario: Checksum mismatch retry
docs.text:
• WHEN the downloaded binary does not match its checksum
  • THEN the entry is downloaded again, and after three failed attempts it is logged as failed and counted as a failure

docs.title: Scenario: Missing archive file
docs.text:
• WHEN the archive returns 404 for a ZIP
  • THEN the entry logs the not-found at debug level and returns no path; the batch loop counts it in the failure counter (there is no separate not-found counter)

docs.title: Scenario: Checksum fetch unavailable
docs.text:
• WHEN the sibling .CHECKSUM fetch raises a connection error or times out
  • THEN the system warns and writes the parquet without verification
  • AND WHEN a checksum request returns a non-200 status (e.g. 404)
  • THEN no log is emitted at all and the parquet is written unverified

docs.title: Requirement: Checkpoint and resume
docs.text: The system SHALL persist a checkpoint JSON file listing the URLs of successfully downloaded entries after every 50 successful downloads and again on shutdown; on restart it SHALL skip already-done URLs. The checkpoint SHALL live at the data root as .download_checkpoint.json, keyed by full URL so spot and usdm entries do not collide. A corrupt or unreadable checkpoint SHALL log a warning, rename the file to a .corrupt sibling, and start over. SIGINT SHALL trigger a graceful shutdown: remaining tasks are canceled, already-finished results are checkpointed, a final checkpoint is saved, and a later invocation resumes.

docs.title: Scenario: Interrupted run resumes
docs.text:
• WHEN a download run is interrupted with Ctrl+C and restarted
  • THEN previously completed URLs are skipped and the run continues from the checkpoint

docs.title: Scenario: Corrupt checkpoint
docs.text:
• WHEN the checkpoint file cannot be parsed
  • THEN the system warns, renames/resets it, and redownloads from scratch without crashing

docs.title: Requirement: Funding-rate REST backfill
docs.text: The funding subcommand SHALL backfill USD-M funding rates from the REST API for the resolved symbol set over the requested months, paginating with a fixed page size and an exclusive cursor (last funding time + 1). Pagination SHALL stop when a page is shorter than the page size or when the cursor passes the requested end; a non-advancing cursor SHALL break the loop instead of looping forever. Rows SHALL be bucketed by UTC day and written as part-backfill.parquet per (day, symbol) under type=funding. Rate-limit responses SHALL be honored via Retry-After, and transient errors SHALL use a bounded backoff. A --dry-run run SHALL print an estimated row count (about 3 rows per symbol per month) and exit.

docs.title: Scenario: Funding dry-run
docs.text:
• WHEN funding runs with --dry-run
  • THEN it prints an estimated row count (roughly months times 3 rows per symbol) and exits without requests

docs.title: Scenario: Non-advancing pagination cursor
docs.text:
• WHEN a funding page returns data that does not advance the cursor
  • THEN the backfill breaks out of the loop instead of continuing forever

docs.title: Scenario: Partial last page
docs.text:
• WHEN a page returns fewer rows than the page size
  • THEN pagination stops because that was the last available funding rate

docs.title: Requirement: Output layout and request policy
docs.text: The system SHALL write parquet under the data root with the partitioned layout market={market}/type={data_type}/dt={YYYY-MM-DD}/symbol={SYM}/part-{granularity}[-{interval}].parquet, where the granularity is monthly or daily and the interval suffix appears for klines only; month-long entries SHALL use dt=YYYY-MM-01. Each entry SHALL be attempted at most three times with an effective backoff of 2 then 5 seconds, the third attempt being terminal (the 15-second value from the shared backoff constant is unused). The pipeline SHALL depend on aiohttp for downloads, pandas/pyarrow for CSV-to-parquet conversion, and the stdlib hashlib/zipfile for verification and unpacking (no aiofiles).

docs.title: Scenario: Monthly dt bucket
docs.text:
• WHEN a monthly entry is written
  • THEN its path uses dt=YYYY-MM-01 and a part name of part-monthly (or part-monthly-1m for klines)

docs.title: Scenario: Daily part naming
docs.text:
• WHEN a daily klines entry for interval 1m is written
  • THEN its parquet part name includes the interval (part-daily-1m.parquet)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines the live trading runtime of alpha_engine (live/): the CLI entry (main.py live-trade), the component wiring in run_live (tick bus, order book manager, snapshot loops, warm-start reader, bar orchestrator), the UTC-aligned BarClock with exchange drift correction (BinanceTimeSync), the signal-only bar evaluation loop (LiveEngine), and the full trader loop (LiveTrader, LiveGoMetricsReader, RiskGuard, OrderExecutor / PaperExecutor / BinanceFuturesExecutor / MakerFuturesExecutor, LiveBlotter, StateStore) driven by the standalone operator entry python -m alpha_engine.live.run_trader. The main.py path is signal-only by contract: signal_only=True is hard-coded at the CLI and any non-signal-only invocation raises NotImplementedError; real execution is reached only through run_trader.

docs.title: Requirement: Live CLI contract
docs.text: The system SHALL expose a live-trade subcommand in the root main.py (and treat a flag-only or empty invocation as live-trade for backwards compatibility) accepting --alphas (nargs+, choices from ALPHA_REGISTRY, default trade_imbalance), --symbols (nargs+, default None meaning the parser's configured SYMBOLS, which is ["BTCUSDT", "ETHUSDT"]), --bar-minutes (default 30), --settlement-seconds (default 5.0), --lookback-days (default 30), --max-w (default 0.03), --end-range (default 50), --market (spot|usdm, default spot), --no-order-book, --snapshot-interval-ms (default None), --data-root (default None, resolved to the data/ directory that sits next to binance_parser/, NOT a CWD-relative path), and --log-level (default INFO; an unrecognised level name falls back to INFO rather than erroring). Symbols SHALL be accepted either as repeated arguments or as a single comma-separated string (parse_symbols), and SHALL be uppercased. The invocation SHALL always run in signal-only mode (Phase 1): no flag exposes execution and run_live(signal_only=False) SHALL raise NotImplementedError. KeyboardInterrupt SHALL print [Main] Stopped. and exit with status 0. The heavy parser imports SHALL be deferred into _run_live so --help does not pull parser dependencies.

docs.title: Scenario: Default invocation
docs.text:
• WHEN python main.py is run with no subcommand
  • THEN it behaves as live-trade with defaults (spot, trade_imbalance, 30-minute bars)

docs.title: Scenario: Execution mode not implemented
docs.text:
• WHEN run_live is called with signal_only=False
  • THEN it raises NotImplementedError (Phases ¾)

docs.title: Scenario: Operator interrupt
docs.text:
• WHEN the operator sends Ctrl-C to a running live-trade
  • THEN the process prints [Main] Stopped. and exits 0 instead of dumping a traceback

docs.title: Requirement: Live service wiring
docs.text:
The system SHALL compose the live runtime in run_live in a fixed order: reject non-signal-only mode; uppercase the symbols; resolve the venue tag (spot -> "binance", usdm -> "binance-f", falling back to the raw market string for an unknown market); build a LiveTickBus and attach a FileWriter sink with exclude_types={"booksnapshot"}; create a single shared HealthCounters that is passed to the OrderBookManager, the WS listener and BinanceTimeSync; build the OrderBookManager only when enable_order_book is true; register an OrderBookUpdatesAggregator as a diff observer when the book is enabled; build LiveRawDataReader with max_lookback_days = lookback_days + 30; warm-start it from parquet under the resolved data root; construct LiveEngineConfig + LiveEngine, a BinanceTimeSync for the market, and a BarClock using bar_minutes and the config's settlement_seconds with time_source=time_sync.now; run the parser's pre-flight symbol validation; print a banner; subscribe the reader to the bus with the publish-edge event filter; then start every long-running task inside one asyncio.TaskGroup.

The task set SHALL be: file writer, time-sync poller, WS listener, and - only when the book is enabled - the order book manager, its watchdog loop, the order-book parquet snapshot loop and the order-book bus snapshot loop; plus the reader consumer and the engine. The parquet snapshot loop SHALL use --snapshot-interval-ms when given and otherwise the parser's LIVE_ORDERBOOK_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_MS (1_800_000 ms = 30 minutes, UTC-aligned), and SHALL be skipped entirely when that effective value is <= 0. The bus snapshot loop SHALL use the parser's LIVE_ORDERBOOK_BUS_INTERVAL_MS (1_000 ms = 1 Hz) only - --snapshot-interval-ms does NOT override it - and SHALL be skipped when that value is <= 0. Both loops sleep to the next epoch-aligned tick, floor the interval at 0.01 s, and snapshot only books that report is_ready(); the parquet loop writes straight to the FileWriter (bypassing the bus) while the bus loop writes to the bus, whose FileWriter sink excludes booksnapshot, so the 1 Hz stream never lands on disk. The bus snapshot loop SHALL keep running because it is the only live source that populates the reader's orderbook deque.

Warm-start SHALL be best effort: a data root that does not exist logs a warning and continues with no warm-start; a successful bootstrap logs the buffer count and total row count and logs an extra warning when 0 rows were loaded; any exception during bootstrap is logged with a traceback and the reader proceeds with empty deques. The OrderBookUpdatesAggregator registration SHALL only keep per-bar diff counters running - nothing consumes flush_for_bar yet, so its metrics do not reach strategies (TODO NSC-48). Because all tasks share one TaskGroup, an unhandled exception in any task SHALL cancel the whole runtime rather than leave a partially-live system.

docs.title: Scenario: Warm-start failure
docs.text:
• WHEN the warm-start bootstrap raises or finds no rows under the data root
  • THEN the runtime logs the failure or a 0-row warning and starts with empty deques rather than aborting

docs.title: Scenario: Book disabled
docs.text:
• WHEN --no-order-book is given
  • THEN no OrderBookManager, watchdog, snapshot loops, or diff-observer are created

docs.title: Scenario: Snapshot interval override scope
docs.text:
• WHEN --snapshot-interval-ms 0 is given
  • THEN the parquet snapshot loop is not started while the 1 Hz bus snapshot loop still runs at LIVE_ORDERBOOK_BUS_INTERVAL_MS

docs.title: Scenario: Soft pre-flight validation
docs.text:
• WHEN the parser's _validate_symbols finds a symbol that is not TRADING, or the exchangeInfo request fails
  • THEN it prints a warning and the runtime proceeds anyway - validation never aborts the run

docs.title: Requirement: Live tick bus
docs.text: The system SHALL fan out every parser event through LiveTickBus, which implements the same write(market, record) contract as the parser's FileWriter so it can serve as the WS listener's writer and as a snapshot-loop writer. Every written event SHALL be offered to each subscriber (one asyncio.Queue each) and then awaited inline on every attached sink, so sinks share the listener's backpressure. Backpressure toward subscribers SHALL be lossy: a subscriber whose queue is full (default 10,000 events, DEFAULT_QUEUE_SIZE) SHALL drop the event, increment its dropped counter, and log a warning only when the drop count is a power of two, while the other subscribers still receive the event. A subscription SHALL optionally restrict event_types at the publish edge so high-rate streams (e.g. raw orderbook diffs) never consume queue slots; events rejected by that filter SHALL NOT count as drops. Sinks SHALL support exclude_types (canonical use: booksnapshot excluded from the parquet writer because the dedicated snapshot loop writes parquet snapshots at a different cadence). The live reader's subscription SHALL be filtered to aggtrades, klines, booksnapshot, funding, markprice, forceorder, trades, deliberately excluding raw orderbook diffs. write SHALL be a no-op once the bus is closed; close() SHALL push a sentinel into every subscription so iteration exits cleanly; flush() SHALL forward to sinks only; start() SHALL be an idle keep-alive loop so a caller can spawn it as a task; and the bus SHALL expose subscriber_count and total_dropped for diagnostics.

docs.title: Scenario: Slow subscriber drop
docs.text:
• WHEN a subscriber's queue fills
  • THEN the event is dropped for that subscriber only, the drop counter increments, and a warning is logged only on power-of-two drop counts

docs.title: Scenario: Publish-edge filter
docs.text:
• WHEN a subscription specifies event_types
  • THEN events outside the set are not enqueued and are not counted as drops, saving queue slots for the events that matter

docs.title: Requirement: Bar clock and time synchronization
docs.text:
BarClock SHALL yield one pd.Timestamp per UTC-aligned bar boundary, strictly after the current time, computed as base + (floor(minutes_into_hour / bar_minutes) + 1) * bar_minutes where minutes_into_hour includes the sub-minute fraction and base is the current hour truncated to minute zero; each yield SHALL be delayed by settlement_seconds (default 5.0) past the boundary so the WS can deliver the last ticks of the just-closed bar, and the sleep SHALL be skipped when the computed wake time is already in the past. bar_minutes <= 0 or settlement_seconds < 0 SHALL raise ValueError. The clock SHALL accept an injectable time_source (default datetime.now(timezone.utc)) so boundaries align to the exchange even on a host with a skewed clock, and it SHALL re-read time_source after computing the boundary so an injected offset is honoured. FakeBarClock SHALL exist as the test harness that yields whatever tick(ts) supplies and stops on close().

BinanceTimeSync SHALL poll the exchange server-time endpoint every poll_interval_sec (default 60) inside a single aiohttp.ClientSession (/api/v3/time on spot base https://api.binance.com, /fapi/v1/time on USD-M base https://fapi.binance.com, 5-second total request timeout), timestamp local time at request start and end and use the midpoint as the local reference, then feed server - local_mid into an EWMA with alpha = 0.3 - except that the FIRST sample is adopted verbatim (no smoothing). It SHALL expose offset_ms() (integer-truncated), now_ms(), now(), has_sample and n_samples. Until the first sample the offset SHALL be 0 (fall back to the local clock); a poll failure SHALL log a warning, return None and keep the previous EWMA rather than resetting. The smoothed absolute drift SHALL be compared against thresholds: over 500 ms (WARN_DRIFT_MS) logs a warning; over 2000 ms (ERROR_DRIFT_MS) logs an error AND calls HealthCounters.record_clock_drift() on the shared counters. Construction SHALL raise ValueError for an unknown market or a non-positive poll interval.

docs.title: Scenario: Settlement delay
docs.text:
• WHEN a bar boundary is reached
  • THEN the clock sleeps settlement_seconds past the boundary before yielding the bar timestamp

docs.title: Scenario: Cold-start clock
docs.text:
• WHEN no server-time sample has landed yet
  • THEN BinanceTimeSync.now() falls back to the local clock unchanged, and the engine still starts immediately

docs.title: Scenario: Transient poll failure
docs.text:
• WHEN a server-time request raises
  • THEN a warning is logged, sample_once returns None, and the previously smoothed offset is retained instead of being reset to 0

docs.title: Requirement: Live raw data reader
docs.text:
LiveRawDataReader SHALL serve the RawDataReader contract (DataFrame views over [since, until], inclusive at both ends, with the same column normalization as the parquet reader) from rolling in-memory deques keyed by (exchange, kind, ticker), fed from a bus subscription tagged with the venue's exchange at consume(...) time. Event routing SHALL be fixed: aggtrades -> trades rows carrying timestamp, price, size, side, agg_id, first_trade_id, last_trade_id; raw trades -> trades_raw (with trade_id) only when the parser flag LIVE_RECONSTRUCT_MULTILEVEL is true, otherwise dropped to prevent double-counting - and if the parser package is not importable the flag SHALL be treated as false with a debug log; forceorder -> liquidations rows (timestamp, side, size from orig_qty, price); klines -> klines rows keyed by open_time with a derived volume_usd = close * volume, and only when the kline is closed; booksnapshot -> long-form orderbook rows, one per bid and ask level at the snapshot timestamp with full depth preserved; funding -> realized_funding only, timestamped by funding_time_ms (the REST row's mark_price is deliberately dropped as a settlement-time snapshot); markprice -> mark_price, index_price, predicted_funding, next_funding_time_ms; and raw orderbook diff updates SHALL be ignored. bootstrap_from SHALL seed the deques from prior parquets for the kinds trades, trades_raw, orderbook, klines, funding, markprice, liquidations, defaulting until to now and since to until - max_lookback.

Eviction SHALL be lazy and two-tiered: read() drops leading rows older than since - eviction_grace (grace default 1 day, no per-kind override on this path), and a periodic global _evict_all runs once evict_every_n_events (default 10,000) rows have accumulated - the counter advances by len(rows) per event, so one full-depth booksnapshot counts as hundreds of rows, not one event - using the per-kind cutoff now - lookback - grace, where KIND_LOOKBACK_OVERRIDES gives orderbook a 1-day lookback while every other kind uses max_lookback_days (constructor default 60; the live service passes lookback_days + 30). read() SHALL return None (not an empty frame) when the key is unknown, the deque is empty after eviction, or the rows carry no timestamp column, and SHALL tz-localize naive timestamps to UTC before slicing. Late-event accounting SHALL count rows whose timestamp is strictly before the last bar passed to mark_bar_processed(bar_ts) (which only ever moves forward), exposing late_events_dropped and logging a warning every late_event_log_every (default 100) additional late rows, so an operator can watch for WS reconnect/load spikes. available_tickers SHALL return the sorted set of tickers seen per (exchange, kind) and buffer_sizes() SHALL expose per-key row counts.

docs.title: Scenario: Double-count protection
docs.text:
• WHEN a raw trades event arrives and LIVE_RECONSTRUCT_MULTILEVEL is off
  • THEN it is routed to nothing, keeping the aggregated trades deque aggtrade-only

docs.title: Scenario: Orderbook memory bound
docs.text:
• WHEN full-depth booksnapshots accumulate
  • THEN the periodic eviction bounds the orderbook deque by a 1-day window while cheaper kinds keep the general lookback window

docs.title: Scenario: Late event accounting
docs.text:
• WHEN an event's timestamp is strictly before the last bar the engine has processed
  • THEN it is counted as late and logged every 100 further late rows, not silently mixed into the wrong bar

docs.title: Scenario: Unknown key read
docs.text:
• WHEN an aggregator reads a (exchange, kind, ticker) triple that has never been seen
  • THEN read returns None rather than an empty DataFrame

docs.title: Requirement: Bar boundary evaluation (signal engine)
docs.text:
LiveEngine SHALL run once per bar: build an ExchangeData view over [bar_ts - lookback_days, bar_ts] via the live reader, run all configured strategies through run_strategies (which itself skips any strategy whose required_kinds are not backed by data, logging a warning), take the latest weight row at or before bar_ts per strategy, then combine - a single surviving strategy passes through as a copy; multiple strategies are blended equal-weight across the sorted union of tickers with missing tickers filled as 0 (PnL-driven Markowitz is deferred). It SHALL then, in order, append (bar_ts, combined) to weights_history, increment bar_count, call reader.mark_bar_processed(bar_ts), and log the bar summary (bar timestamp, bar number, strategy count, gross, non-zero count, cumulative late-event count) - the weight vector itself is never logged - and return the combined Series.

Failure handling SHALL be narrow by design: only the run_strategies call is wrapped, so a strategy exception logs and returns None, and a bar where no strategy produced a usable row logs and returns None. In both None cases bar_count, weights_history and mark_bar_processed SHALL be left untouched. LiveEngine.run SHALL simply iterate the bar clock and await step, with NO catch-all - an exception raised outside run_strategies (e.g. in the blend) propagates and, via the shared TaskGroup, tears the runtime down. LiveEngineConfig defaults SHALL be exchanges=["binance", "binance-f"], max_w=0.03, end_range=50, lookback_days=30, settlement_seconds=5.0.

docs.title: Scenario: Multiple strategies blend
docs.text:
• WHEN two or more strategies produce weights for a bar
  • THEN the target is the equal-weight average of their latest rows across the union of tickers

docs.title: Scenario: Strategy failure is not fatal
docs.text:
• WHEN run_strategies raises at a bar
  • THEN the bar logs the exception, returns None, and neither the bar counter nor the late-event boundary advances; the loop keeps running

docs.title: Requirement: Go metrics window reader for the trader
docs.text: LiveGoMetricsReader SHALL serve the trader a GoExchangeData over [bar_ts - lookback_days, bar_ts] built from the Go parser's market=<market>/type=metrics parquet (market default usdm), by default rebuilding a GoMetricsStore per bar. Disk caching SHALL default to OFF (cache_dir=None) because the store's cache key contains the moving (since, until) window, so a live cache never hits while rewriting most frames per bar. preload_window(since, until) SHALL load one store for a whole offline run; subsequent exchange_data calls whose window falls inside the preloaded range SHALL be served as a _SlicedExchangeData view that truncates every frame to [since, until] (so frame.iloc[-1] lands on the bar with no look-ahead), while any window outside the preloaded range SHALL fall back to building a fresh store. latest_metric_ts() SHALL scan dt= partitions newest-first, skip empty days with only a directory glob, return the max ts of the first populated day as a UTC timestamp, log a warning and skip a day whose shards are unreadable, and return None when no metrics exist. The result SHALL be cached after the first successful scan and never refreshed for the rest of the process - correct for offline dry-runs where the newest on-disk bar does not move, but in a live run the dashboard's parser_last_metric_ts reflects the state at first call, not the newest bar.

docs.title: Scenario: Offline preload
docs.text:
• WHEN preload_window has covered the run and the trader asks for a bar inside it
  • THEN the reader returns a cheap in-memory sliced view instead of re-reading the lake

docs.title: Scenario: Unreadable metrics day
docs.text:
• WHEN the newest populated dt= partition has a corrupt shard
  • THEN latest_metric_ts logs a warning and continues to the next-older day instead of raising

docs.title: Requirement: Trader bar loop
docs.text:
LiveTrader.step SHALL run the full round-trip bar: read the metrics window from LiveGoMetricsReader, compute the target via an injectable weight_fn, resolve prices, reconcile, risk-check, trade, re-reconcile and persist state, in that order.

make_portfolio_weight_fn SHALL be the default weight function: run the named alphas via run_strategies (returning None when no strategy ran); pass a single strategy through; for multiple strategies call combine_strategies with prices taken from the hard-coded data["binance-f"]["mark_price"] frame (NOT TraderConfig.price_key), method=combine (default risk_parity - the estimation-free default, since on short histories the Markowitz tangency chases noise; markowitz and ew are the other choices) and lookback=mk_lookback_bars (default 48 * 30 bars). Only ValueError and numpy.linalg.LinAlgError from the combiner SHALL be caught, logged and turned into a HOLD (None); any other exception propagates. It SHALL then take the last row at or before bar_ts, dropna() it, and return None if empty. A predictability freshness guard SHALL then drop symbols whose order-book metrics are frozen - fewer than 2 distinct values over the last 6 bars of ob__minor__imbalance_top25__mean on the binance-f frame - and if the lookup itself fails or the recent window is empty the guard SHALL be skipped entirely (every symbol kept); if every symbol is stale it SHALL log and HOLD (None) instead of emitting an empty target that would liquidate the book. Only after the guard SHALL target_leverage > 0 rescale the book so sum|w| == target_leverage.

step SHALL treat None as "no opinion this bar - HOLD the current book": the target becomes an empty Series, no rebalance is issued, and the log line is suffixed HOLD; an explicit (possibly empty) Series is a real target and an empty one flattens every position - the two cases SHALL stay distinct so warm-up or degenerate input cannot accidentally flatten a live book. Prices SHALL be taken from the last row of data["binance-f"][price_key] (TraderConfig.price_key, default mark_price) over the union of that row's index, the target index and the currently held symbols, keeping only finite strictly-positive values. executor.reconcile SHALL run BEFORE the risk check so equity, positions and daily drawdown reflect venue reality, and again after trading so an ambiguous fill self-corrects before the snapshot is persisted; mark_to_market follows each reconcile. Trading SHALL happen only when the price map is non-empty: a latched kill-switch rebalances toward an empty target (an immediate flatten that bypasses smoothing), otherwise a decision that is neither held nor a HOLD rebalances toward _smooth_toward(decision.approved_weights, prices). Execution smoothing SHALL move from the blotter's current marked weights toward the approved target by at most smooth_delta (TraderConfig.smooth_delta, default 0.005, 0/None disables) per symbol per bar, dropping exactly-zero entries from the result; an empty target still winds down at the same rate. step SHALL then increment bar_count, record the fills, and write the state file with decision.approved_weights as target_weights and reader.latest_metric_ts() as parser_last_metric_ts. LiveTrader.run SHALL wrap each bar in a catch-all that logs LiveTrader.step failed at <bar> and continues, so an exception in the weight function, executor, reconcile or state write never kills the loop (state is simply not persisted for that bar).

docs.title: Scenario: Stale-book freshness guard
docs.text:
• WHEN a symbol's ob__minor__imbalance_top25__mean is identical across the last 6 bars (dead depth stream)
  • THEN the symbol is dropped from the target before leverage scaling; if every symbol is stale the loop holds the book

docs.title: Scenario: HOLD vs flatten
docs.text:
• WHEN the combiner is degenerate during warm-up and raises ValueError or LinAlgError
  • THEN the weight function returns None (hold the book) rather than an empty target that would liquidate every position

docs.title: Scenario: Execution smoothing
docs.text:
• WHEN the target moves by more than smooth_delta per symbol
  • THEN the executor receives only the clipped step toward the target (except the kill-switch flatten path, which bypasses smoothing because safety exits must be immediate)

docs.title: Scenario: No usable prices
docs.text:
• WHEN the price frame yields no finite positive price for the bar
  • THEN no rebalance is attempted at all, yet the bar is still counted and the state file is still written

docs.title: Requirement: Risk guard
docs.text: Every target weight vector SHALL pass through RiskGuard.check before execution, failing safe toward less risk and in this order: roll the blotter's day reference when ts is given; return a flat, nav_usd=0.0, killed=True decision if the kill-switch is already latched; latch the kill-switch and return the same flat decision when blotter.daily_drawdown() <= -abs(max_daily_drawdown_pct) (0.02); return a held decision carrying the blotter's current actual weights reindexed onto the target's index when min_rebalance_seconds > 0 and the previous rebalance was more recent than that (the knob defaults to 0.0, i.e. the rate limit is disabled unless explicitly configured); then scrub non-finite weights to 0; clip |w_i| to max_per_symbol_pct (0.05); scale the whole vector down when gross sum|w| exceeds max_total_leverage (1.0); and record - without correcting - a violation when |sum w| exceeds max_net_exposure (0.20). NAV SHALL be min(blotter.equity, max_nav_usd) (default 200.0) and is 0.0 on both kill paths. _last_rebalance_ts SHALL be updated at the end of any non-kill, non-held check where ts was supplied, whether or not trading actually follows. Every applied correction SHALL append a human-readable string to RiskDecision.violations, which the state file publishes. The kill-switch SHALL latch permanently until reset() is called by an operator, and SHALL be re-appliable from persisted state on restart via latch(), so a crash cannot silently re-arm trading inside a losing day.

docs.title: Scenario: Kill-switch latch
docs.text:
• WHEN the daily drawdown breaches the threshold
  • THEN the kill-switch latches and every later check returns a flat target with nav_usd=0.0 until an operator resets it

docs.title: Scenario: Rate-limited hold
docs.text:
• WHEN two rebalances land within min_rebalance_seconds and that knob is greater than 0
  • THEN the second is a held decision carrying the current actual weights, so nothing trades

docs.title: Requirement: Order sizing and paper execution
docs.text: The system SHALL express execution through the abstract OrderExecutor, whose rebalance diffs a target against the current book and whose reconcile defaults to a no-op (paper trading has no external venue and its blotter is authoritative). target_quantities(weights, prices, nav) SHALL map each weight to w * nav / price and SHALL yield 0.0 for a None/NaN weight or a missing, non-positive or NaN price. PaperExecutor SHALL mark to market, compute target quantities, walk the sorted union of target symbols and currently held symbols, skip any symbol without a valid positive price (so a held position with no price cannot be closed that bar), and trade only the delta, skipping any delta whose notional is below min_notional_usd (class default 5.0). Fills SHALL be modelled at price * (1 + sign(delta) * slippage_bps / 1e4) (class default 1.0 bps, charged against the trade direction) with a fee of |delta| * fill_price * fee_rate (class default 1.6e-4), mirroring the backtest cost model so paper PnL tracks backtest net PnL. Note that run_trader constructs PaperExecutor from its own CLI defaults (--fee-bps 4.0 -> 4e-4, --slippage-bps 1.0, --min-notional 5.0), so the operator-facing fee default is 4 bps, not the class default.

docs.title: Scenario: Dust skipped
docs.text:
• WHEN the delta for a symbol is below min_notional_usd in notional terms
  • THEN no order is placed for that symbol

docs.title: Scenario: Unpriced holding
docs.text:
• WHEN a currently held symbol has no valid price in the bar's price map
  • THEN the paper executor skips it entirely rather than filling at a bogus price

docs.title: Requirement: Binance USD-M futures client
docs.text: BinanceFuturesClient SHALL be testnet-by-default: the base URL is https://testnet.binancefuture.com unless testnet=False, which selects https://fapi.binance.com. Signed requests SHALL append timestamp and recvWindow (default 5000) and an HMAC-SHA256 signature over the urlencoded parameters, and SHALL be sent with the X-MBX-APIKEY header; public requests SHALL send no headers. The HTTP transport SHALL be injectable (default requests with a 10-second timeout and raise_for_status, imported lazily) so signing and rebalance logic are testable without a network. The client SHALL keep a venue clock offset: sync_time() samples /fapi/v1/time, RTT-corrects via the request midpoint, warns when the host is more than 1000 ms off, and on failure keeps the previous offset while still backing off; _signed SHALL auto-sync when no explicit time_fn was injected and the last sync is older than SYNC_INTERVAL_S (1800 s). Endpoints SHALL cover /fapi/v2/account, /fapi/v2/positionRisk (non-flat positions only), /fapi/v1/premiumIndex mark prices (unparseable rows warn and are omitted), /fapi/v1/income with incomeType=TRANSFER and limit=1000 for day transfers, /fapi/v1/exchangeInfo filters (step_size, min_qty, min_notional from MIN_NOTIONAL or NOTIONAL, tick_size, qty_precision, price_precision, status), /fapi/v1/leverageBracket (the per-symbol MINIMUM notionalCap, best effort - a failure logs a warning and returns an empty map), POST /fapi/v1/order for MARKET and GTX/GTC LIMIT orders with newOrderRespType=RESULT (so the response carries the final executed qty and average price instead of a bare ACK), GET/DELETE /fapi/v1/order, /fapi/v1/ticker/bookTicker, and /fapi/v1/userTrades. Quantities SHALL be serialised as fixed-point strings because Binance rejects scientific notation, and round_step SHALL round magnitude DOWN to the step while preserving sign.

docs.title: Scenario: Testnet by default
docs.text:
• WHEN a client is constructed without testnet=False
  • THEN every request targets testnet.binancefuture.com; mainnet must be chosen explicitly

docs.title: Scenario: Clock offset compensation
docs.text:
• WHEN the host clock has drifted and a signed request is about to be sent more than 1800 s after the last sync
  • THEN the client re-syncs against /fapi/v1/time and signs with the offset-corrected timestamp, so orders do not fail with -1021

docs.title: Requirement: Real futures execution and reconciliation
docs.text:
BinanceFuturesExecutor SHALL rebalance real USD-M positions toward the target. Until the first successful account mirror (_reconciled_once), rebalance SHALL log a warning and return no orders rather than size a restart book off the blank initial snapshot. It SHALL lazily load exchange filters once (attaching max_notional_cap from the leverage brackets, with a warning when brackets are unavailable), mark to market, and read the venue's signed positions as the source of truth for "current". Positions whose symbol vanished from the universe SHALL be priced from mark_prices() so their target (0) still values them for closing (orphan guard); if that call fails the executor SHALL log an error and leave those positions unmanaged. Per symbol it SHALL skip symbols without a valid price, skip symbols absent from exchangeInfo or whose status is not TRADING, cap the TARGET notional to max_notional_cap so a thin symbol cannot trigger a -2027 "exceeded max position at current leverage" rejection, diff against the venue position, round the delta DOWN to step_size, additionally clamp it to qty_precision decimals when the step size was missing (avoiding -1111), skip a zero delta, and skip any delta whose notional is below max(config.min_notional_usd, filter min_notional). reduce_only SHALL be sent only when reduce_only_on_decrease is enabled and the trade strictly shrinks a same-signed position.

Order failures SHALL never retry: a -1007/408/timeout body logs a warning and is left for the post-rebalance reconcile (the order may have executed, so a retry risks a double fill); any other error logs at error level; both continue to the next symbol. Fills SHALL be booked from executedQty and avgPrice (falling back to the bar price), with a zero-executed response logged as "order not filled" and left for reconcile. Fees SHALL come from /fapi/v1/userTrades for the order when every commission is paid in a quote asset (USDT, USDC, BUSD, FDUSD), otherwise from the response's fills[] commissions, otherwise estimated as notional * default_fee_rate (4e-4 taker, 2e-4 maker).

reconcile SHALL overwrite the blotter from one /fapi/v2/account call - positions with entry prices, totalMarginBalance as equity, totalWalletBalance as wallet, totalUnrealizedProfit as unrealized - plus today's net transfers from day_transfers since UTC midnight (a failure there logs a warning and keeps the previous transfer adjustment), and SHALL set _reconciled_once. An account() API error SHALL be swallowed with a warning, keeping local state; but an unparseable positionAmt SHALL log an error and RE-RAISE out of reconcile (rather than silently dropping a live position), which aborts the bar via LiveTrader.run's catch-all and leaves _reconciled_once unchanged. An unparseable entryPrice SHALL warn and fall back to 0.0.

docs.title: Scenario: Restart reconciliation
docs.text:
• WHEN the executor starts with an already-open venue position
  • THEN the first rebalance is skipped until reconcile succeeds, after which it trades only the difference between the venue's position and the target, never re-opening the full position

docs.title: Scenario: Ambiguous order timeout
docs.text:
• WHEN an order request fails with -1007/timeout
  • THEN the executor logs a warning, does not retry, and lets the post-rebalance reconcile read the venue's real position

docs.title: Requirement: Maker (post-only) execution
docs.text: MakerFuturesExecutor SHALL extend the futures executor by replacing the single market order with a post-only-first flow: price at the touch on our own side (best bid for BUY, best ask for SELL) from bookTicker, rounded DOWN to tick_size and formatted to price_precision, and post a GTX limit. A GTX bounce - the venue rejecting with -5022/"Post Only" or the response reporting status EXPIRED - SHALL be repriced and re-posted up to reprice_attempts (default 2, floored at 1 attempt) and only then fall back to a market order; any other order exception SHALL propagate to the caller's per-symbol error handler. A resting order SHALL be polled every poll_seconds (default 2.0) until its status is one of FILLED, CANCELED, EXPIRED, REJECTED or wait_seconds (default 45.0) elapses, with a failed poll logged and the previous state retained; a still-open order is then cancelled and the remainder sent to market. If the cancel races a fill (-2011) the order SHALL be re-queried; if BOTH the cancel and the re-query fail the final state is unknown and the market fallback SHALL be deliberately skipped (fail-closed - the order is left for the next reconcile to settle). The market fallback SHALL size only qty - executedQty, rounded down to the step, and SHALL be skipped when that remainder is below max(min_notional_usd, filter min_notional). MakerExecConfig SHALL inherit the futures config and default default_fee_rate to 2e-4 (maker).

docs.title: Scenario: GTX bounce reprice
docs.text:
• WHEN the venue rejects the post-only limit as crossing, or returns status EXPIRED
  • THEN the executor reprices at the new touch and retries up to reprice_attempts before falling back to a market order

docs.title: Scenario: Unknown final state fails closed
docs.text:
• WHEN both the cancel and the follow-up query of a resting maker order fail
  • THEN no market fallback is sent and the order is left for the next reconcile to settle

docs.title: Requirement: Position and PnL accounting
docs.text:
LiveBlotter SHALL require a positive initial_capital and book every fill with the average-cost method: same-direction (or from-flat) fills recompute the weighted average entry; reducing, closing, or flipping fills realize (exit_price - avg_entry) * closed_qty * direction on the closed quantity; a position within 1e-15 of zero snaps to flat with a zero entry; a flip leaves the leftover quantity at the fill price. apply_fill SHALL raise ValueError on a negative fee or a NaN quantity/price, SHALL accumulate per-symbol and total fees, SHALL update that symbol's mark to the fill price, and SHALL append to the fill log. mark_to_market SHALL ignore missing, NaN or non-positive prices.

In paper mode equity SHALL be initial_capital + realized + unrealized - total_fees, with unrealized marked from the latest prices (falling back to the average entry when no mark exists). In live-venue mode the exchange is the source of truth: after reconcile_from_exchange the equity is the venue's margin balance, realized PnL becomes wallet - initial_capital, and unrealized is the venue's figure - all WITHOUT corrupting initial_capital (kept as the true deposit so PnL stays meaningful). Flat or NaN venue positions SHALL be dropped from the mirrored book. Leverage SHALL be gross_exposure / equity, or infinity when equity is non-positive, and actual_weights SHALL return all-zero weights when equity is non-positive. The daily drawdown reference SHALL reset at each UTC date change (roll_day_if_needed, which also zeroes the day's transfers), be restorable from persisted state on restart (restore_day_reference), and adjust for net wallet transfers so deposits are not profit and withdrawals are not loss; the result SHALL be clamped to <= 0 and SHALL be 0.0 when the day reference or the deposit-adjusted base is non-positive. snapshot() SHALL return a plain dict (including day_utc, day_start_equity, n_fills and a per-symbol position table) consumed by the dashboard and the state file.

docs.title: Scenario: Average-cost entry
docs.text:
• WHEN a position is increased in the same direction
  • THEN the average entry price is recalculated weighted by the new fill; realized PnL is not booked

docs.title: Scenario: Flip realized PnL
docs.text:
• WHEN a fill flips a position from long to short
  • THEN realized PnL books on the closed long quantity and the leftover short opens at the fill price

docs.title: Scenario: Deposit-adjusted drawdown
docs.text:
• WHEN a mid-day wallet transfer is mirrored from the venue
  • THEN the daily drawdown nets the transfer out of today's PnL and out of the capital base, so a deposit cannot blind the kill-switch and a withdrawal cannot false-trigger it

docs.title: Requirement: State contract for the dashboard
docs.text: The system SHALL persist one JSON state file per run, written atomically (a temp file created in the same directory, then os.replace; on any failure the temp file is unlinked and the error re-raised) once per bar - fills are folded into the same bar's update via record_fills and there is no fill-triggered write - with the schema: updated_ts, mode, bar_count, last_bar_ts, next_bar_eta_s, parser_last_metric_ts, killed, risk_violations, account (initial_capital/equity/realized_pnl/unrealized_pnl/total_fees/gross_exposure/leverage/ daily_drawdown/day_utc/day_start_equity/n_fills), positions[], target_weights, actual_weights, equity_curve (capped at 5000 points), recent_fills (capped at 200), and weight_history (capped at 96 entries, about 48 h of 30-minute bars). target_weights SHALL be serialised as a dict with NaN and exactly-zero entries removed. The equity-curve and weight-history points SHALL be appended only when bar_ts is not None. The parent directory SHALL be created on construction. JSON SHALL be written with allow_nan=False, so a non-finite value in the snapshot raises rather than emitting invalid JSON. A restart SHALL seed the rolling history from the existing file (so the equity curve, fills tape and weight tape survive frequent restarts); an unreadable or corrupt file SHALL log a warning and start empty rather than crash, and individual malformed history entries SHALL be skipped. StateStore.read SHALL return an empty dict for a missing file. The file SHALL be read-only for the dashboard process and never written by it.

docs.title: Scenario: Restart seeding
docs.text:
• WHEN the trader restarts and a state file exists
  • THEN equity curve, recent fills, and weight history are pre-seeded from the file

docs.title: Scenario: Corrupt state file
docs.text:
• WHEN the state file is unreadable at startup
  • THEN the trader warns and continues with empty history instead of crashing

docs.title: Requirement: Standalone trader entry
docs.text:
The system SHALL provide an operator entry point (python -m alpha_engine.live.run_trader) with explicit safety-ordered modes --mode paper|testnet|mainnet (paper default, no exchange contact; mainnet additionally logs a warning naming the NAV cap, leverage and DD kill), a required repeatable --metrics-root, and these defaults: --market usdm, --symbols "" (comma-separated; empty means all), --alphas book_depth_imbalance (comma-separated), --combine risk_parity (markowitz|risk_parity|ew), --price-key mark_price, --capital 10000.0, --max-nav 200.0, --max-per-symbol 0.05, --max-leverage 1.0, --target-leverage 0.0, --max-daily-dd 0.02, --fee-bps 4.0, --slippage-bps 1.0, --min-notional 5.0, --execution taker, --maker-wait 45.0, --lookback-days 30, --alloc-lookback-days 14, --smooth-delta 0.005 (0 disables), --state-file live_state.json, --reset-kill, --bars 0, --bar-minutes 30, --log-level INFO. The combiner's bar lookback SHALL be derived as alloc_lookback_days * (1440 // bar_minutes). An empty --alphas list SHALL leave weight_fn unset so LiveTrader builds the default one from its config. min_rebalance_seconds SHALL NOT be exposed, so the risk guard's rate limit stays disabled.

--bars N SHALL run an offline dry-run: anchor on latest_metric_ts() floored to the bar size (exiting with SystemExit when no metrics exist), build the last N bar timestamps, preload the whole window once, step each bar without waiting on boundaries or contacting an exchange, and print a completion line with the final equity and the state-file path. Otherwise the run SHALL be live on a BarClock with settlement_seconds = 10.0 (the CLI and BarClock default of 5.0 does not apply here); when the executor exposes a client with offset_ms (testnet/mainnet), client.sync_time() SHALL be called on startup and a time_source SHALL shift the local clock by client.offset_ms() so bar boundaries align to the venue - in paper mode no client exists and the local clock is used unchanged. --execution SHALL select the rebalance flow: taker uses BinanceFuturesExecutor, maker uses MakerFuturesExecutor with --maker-wait as its rest window. Testnet and mainnet SHALL read BINANCE_API_KEY / BINANCE_API_SECRET from the environment and SHALL exit with SystemExit when either is missing.

On startup the runtime SHALL re-apply persisted safety state, but only when the persisted mode matches the current --mode (safety state never leaks across paper/testnet/mainnet): a previously latched kill-switch SHALL stay latched with a CRITICAL log unless --reset-kill is given (which logs a warning and re-arms), and the persisted day-start drawdown baseline SHALL be restored only when its day_utc is the current UTC day (a next-day restart deliberately skips the restore, since a stale baseline would corrupt the new day's drawdown reference) - so a crash-restart inside a losing day cannot silently reset the daily kill reference.

docs.title: Scenario: Offline dry-run
docs.text:
• WHEN --bars N is given
  • THEN the trader preloads the metrics window once and runs over the latest N metric bars without waiting on bar boundaries and without exchange contact

docs.title: Scenario: Persisted kill-switch survives restart
docs.text:
• WHEN the trader restarts inside a losing day and the persisted state has killed: true and the same mode
  • THEN the kill-switch stays latched unless --reset-kill is given, and the day's drawdown baseline is restored so the daily kill can still fire

docs.title: Scenario: Missing API credentials
docs.text:
• WHEN --mode testnet or --mode mainnet is used without BINANCE_API_KEY and BINANCE_API_SECRET
  • THEN the process exits with SystemExit before any executor is constructed

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines the live WebSocket pipeline of binance_parser: the live CLI entry point, per-market subscription sets, connection and reconnect policy, stream dispatch to parquet, buffered writer semantics, local order-book lifecycle and snapshots, health/stats accounting, and task composition of the live run.

docs.title: Requirement: Live CLI contract
docs.text: The system SHALL expose a live subcommand accepting --market (spot|usdm|both, default spot), --symbols (space-separated, default BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT, upper-cased), --order-book (flag), and --with-funding (flag). The command SHALL run until interrupted, and a keyboard interrupt SHALL stop it with exit code 0.

docs.title: Scenario: Default live run
docs.text:
• WHEN the live command is run with no flags
  • THEN it starts a spot-market pipeline for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT without the order book or funding poller

docs.title: Scenario: Symbols upper-cased
docs.text:
• WHEN symbols are passed in lowercase
  • THEN the pipeline operates on the upper-cased symbols

docs.title: Requirement: Stream subscription sets
docs.text: The system SHALL subscribe per symbol, per market, to a fixed stream set: always @depth, @aggTrade, and @kline_1m; plus, on usdm only, @markPrice@1s and (when enabled) @forceOrder. The raw @trade stream SHALL be subscribed only when trades are preferred over aggregate trades (or multilevel reconstruction is enabled); by default it is not subscribed and aggregate trades are the canonical trade source.

docs.title: Scenario: Default spot subscription
docs.text:
• WHEN a spot listener starts for a symbol with default settings
  • THEN exactly @depth, @aggTrade, and @kline_1m streams are subscribed

docs.title: Scenario: Default usdm subscription
docs.text:
• WHEN a usdm listener starts for a symbol with default settings
  • THEN @depth, @aggTrade, @kline_1m, @markPrice@1s, and @forceOrder are subscribed

docs.title: Scenario: Raw trades opt-in
docs.text:
• WHEN aggregate-trade preference is disabled
  • THEN @trade is additionally subscribed and raw fills are written as trades events alongside aggtrades

docs.title: Requirement: WebSocket persistence semantics
docs.text: The system SHALL persist via the writer only: aggtrades, closed klines, markprice (usdm), forceorder (usdm, when enabled), trades (when subscribed), and booksnapshot (order-book snapshots). Depth diffs SHALL never be persisted: they feed only the in-process order book and health counters. Running (unclosed) klines and unknown streams SHALL be dropped silently.

docs.title: Scenario: Depth diff bypass
docs.text:
• WHEN a @depth message arrives and an order-book manager is present
  • THEN it is routed to the book manager and health counters only, and the writer is never invoked

docs.title: Scenario: Depth-diff debug logging hook
docs.text:
• WHEN the depth-log interval setting is configured to a positive value
  • THEN the first and then every Nth depth diff per stream is logged at debug level

docs.title: Scenario: Malformed-frame resilience
docs.text:
• WHEN an incoming frame fails to parse with JSONDecodeError, KeyError, or ValueError (bad JSON, missing keys, wrong value types)
  • THEN the frame is logged with the error trace and skipped, and the WS connection deliberately survives; other unexpected exceptions are treated as code bugs and escalate (abort the run) rather than being masked by a reconnect

docs.title: Scenario: Silent unknown-stream drop
docs.text:
• WHEN a message matches no known stream
  • THEN it is ignored without failing the connection

docs.title: Requirement: WebSocket reconnect policy
docs.text: The system SHALL reconnect a closed or failed connection with exponential backoff starting at 1 second and doubling, capped at 60 seconds, reset to 1 on any successful connection. The connection SHALL keep an application-level heartbeat (ping every 20 seconds, timeout 10 seconds, close timeout 5 seconds). After 30 consecutive reconnect failures the listener SHALL raise an error to its supervisor instead of retrying forever. Unexpected (non-network) exceptions SHALL propagate immediately, never being masked as reconnects. Every reconnect except the first SHALL be recorded with the disconnection gap.

docs.title: Scenario: Backoff reset on success
docs.text:
• WHEN a connection attempt succeeds after prior failures
  • THEN the backoff timer resets to 1 second and the failure counter clears

docs.title: Scenario: Give-up escalation
docs.text:
• WHEN 30 consecutive reconnect attempts fail
  • THEN the listener raises a runtime error describing the failure count

docs.title: Scenario: Code error escalation
docs.text:
• WHEN a frame handler raises an unexpected exception
  • THEN the exception propagates immediately and the loop does not attempt a reconnect

docs.title: Requirement: Buffered parquet writer
docs.text: The system SHALL buffer records in memory and flush them to parquet under a Hive-partitioned layout: data/market={m}/type={t}/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol={SYM}/part-*.parquet. Flush SHALL trigger when the total buffered record count reaches 100,000 or a 60-second timer elapses. At flush, records SHALL be grouped by their own event-UTC-date so buckets straddling midnight land in the correct dt= partition. Writes SHALL use zstd compression (level 3), write to a sibling temp file, and atomically replace the target path. A failed partition write SHALL be retried (3 attempts, escalating backoff) and the failure SHALL be raised after the flush completes the remaining partitions.

docs.title: Scenario: Midnight partition correctness
docs.text:
• WHEN a flush contains records whose event times fall on different UTC dates
  • THEN each record lands in the parquet file of its own event date partition

docs.title: Scenario: Atomic part write
docs.text:
• WHEN a parquet part is written
  • THEN it is first written to a temporary sibling file and then atomically renamed, so a crash never leaves a corrupt file at the canonical path

docs.title: Scenario: Flush by record count
docs.text:
• WHEN the total buffered record count reaches 100,000 before the 60-second timer
  • THEN a flush occurs immediately

docs.title: Requirement: Order-book state lifecycle
docs.text: The system SHALL maintain one in-memory order book per (market, symbol), seeded from a REST depth snapshot and kept in sync with @depth diffs. The book SHALL have states bootstrapping, live, and resyncing. Spot and usdm SHALL apply the venue-specific contiguity rules: spot drops diffs with u <= snapshot id, bridges when U <= snapshot id + 1 <= u, and requires U == previous u + 1; usdm drops diffs with u < snapshot id, bridges when U <= snapshot id <= u, and requires pu == previous u. A level with quantity zero SHALL remove the level. A non-contiguous live diff SHALL move the book to resyncing and re-bootstrap.

docs.title: Scenario: Level removal by zero quantity
docs.text:
• WHEN a diff carries a level with quantity zero
  • THEN the corresponding price level is removed from the book

docs.title: Scenario: Gap triggers resync
docs.text:
• WHEN a live diff is not contiguous with the previous one
  • THEN the book transitions to resyncing, the gap is counted, and a re-bootstrap is scheduled

docs.title: Scenario: Usdm overlapping ranges tolerated
docs.text:
• WHEN a usdm diff overlaps the previous range instead of extending it exactly
  • THEN the diff is applied and the book remains live (usdm contiguity is defined by pu)

docs.title: Scenario: Diff observers
docs.text:
• WHEN observers are registered on a live book and a diff arrives
  • THEN each observer is invoked before the diff is applied, with the touched price levels and the mid price; an observer failure is logged and never interrupts the dispatch loop

docs.title: Requirement: Order-book bootstrap
docs.text: The system SHALL bootstrap a book by fetching the venue's deepest snapshot (spot up to 5000 levels, usdm up to 1000), then replaying buffered diffs sorted by final update id: stale diffs dropped, the first surviving diff must bridge the snapshot, and subsequent diffs must be contiguous, else bootstrap repeats. Cold-start snapshot fetches SHALL be staggered per symbol (spot 2.5s, usdm 0.5s) with at most 2 concurrent fetches. USD-M snapshot fetches SHALL charge the shared rate limiter (weight 20 at max depth); spot bootstrap in the standalone run passes no limiter and relies on the stagger plus the concurrency cap. A 200 response without lastUpdateId (delisted or renamed symbol) SHALL raise an error that is absorbed by the retry backoff. Rate-limit responses SHALL be honored via Retry-After plus 5-30 seconds of jitter; other failures SHALL back off exponentially to 30 seconds.

docs.title: Scenario: Snapshot-limited bootstrap
docs.text:
• WHEN a book cannot bridge the snapshot with the buffered diffs
  • THEN bootstrap is retried after a fixed 2-second wait and the book keeps its current state: a cold-start book stays bootstrapping, while a book that fell behind after going live stays resyncing (bootstrap itself never sets the state, it only flips to live on success)

docs.title: Scenario: Rate-limited bootstrap wait
docs.text:
• WHEN a depth snapshot fetch returns 429 or 418
  • THEN the retry sleeps for the response's Retry-After plus a random 5-30 second jitter

docs.title: Scenario: Buffered diffs after failed bridge
docs.text:
• WHEN a bootstrap attempt fails contiguity after applying the bridging diff
  • THEN the buffered diffs are discarded and the next bootstrap re-seeds from a fresh snapshot (only the no-bridge case keeps the buffer)

docs.title: Scenario: Watchdog force-resync
docs.text:
• WHEN a live book receives no diffs for more than 30 seconds, or a resyncing book stays resyncing for more than 60 seconds
  • THEN the watchdog forces a resync and counts it

docs.title: Requirement: Order-book snapshots
docs.text: The system SHALL persist the full book (bids and asks as parallel float32 price/size arrays, one row per event, carrying also the symbol, snapshot timestamp, and the book's last update id) into type=booksnapshot partitions at a UTC-aligned cadence of 30 minutes (configurable; zero disables persistence), i.e. at :00 and :30 UTC, 48 snapshots per symbol per day. Only books in live state SHALL be snapshotted; a half-bootstrapped book SHALL be skipped. A separate 1-second in-process bus snapshot loop SHALL exist for metric consumers and SHALL never touch disk; it is not started in standalone parser runs.

docs.title: Scenario: UTC-aligned snapshot ticks
docs.text:
• WHEN the snapshot loop runs with the default 30-minute interval
  • THEN snapshots are written at :00 and :30 UTC regardless of process start time

docs.title: Scenario: Unready book skipped
docs.text:
• WHEN a book is not in live state at snapshot time
  • THEN no snapshot row is written for it for that tick

docs.title: Scenario: Snapshot persistence disabled
docs.text:
• WHEN the snapshot interval is set to zero
  • THEN no booksnapshot parquet files are written and a notice is printed

docs.title: Requirement: Health and pipeline statistics
docs.text: The system SHALL track health counters (trade-id gaps - incremented only for raw @trade events when a trade id is not exactly the previous plus one; since the default subscription prefers @aggTrade and the raw @trade stream is not subscribed by default, this counter stays at zero unless raw trades are explicitly enabled; WS reconnects; order-book force resyncs; plus a clock-drift counter that the parser's own live run never increments - the standalone run leaves it at zero, and the only caller of record_clock_drift() is the alpha-engine live time-sync process) and per-symbol last-event timestamps. It SHALL expose a Python snapshot of these counters via the health object's snapshot method for in-process consumers; no HTTP or metrics endpoint exists (a Prometheus exporter is intentionally excluded). The pipeline SHALL report periodic statistics: message counts and lag per stream, reconnect count, and depth-resync counts per symbol, reported every 60 seconds; a high-frequency stream (aggtrades) that has never delivered a message, or whose lag exceeds 10 times its 30-second threshold (i.e. 300 seconds), SHALL trigger a warning.

docs.title: Scenario: Trade id gap detection
docs.text:
• WHEN a trade arrives whose id is not the previously seen id plus one
  • THEN the trade-id-gap counter increments and a warning is logged

docs.title: Scenario: Silent stream warning
docs.text:
• WHEN the aggtrades stream has never received a message after the first report, or its lag exceeds 300 seconds (10 times its 30-second threshold)
  • THEN the reporter logs a stream-silent or stream-lag warning

docs.title: Requirement: Live run composition
docs.text: The system SHALL run the live pipeline as a task group sharing one writer, one stats object, one health object, and one shared USD-M rate limiter across all components.
