  • THEN book_updates_count equals book_resync_count (one per snapshot seen so far) and book_seq_gaps is always 0

docs.title: Requirement: Rolling ring buffer
docs.text: The system SHALL keep the window of 1-second slots in a fixed-capacity ring (Ring, capacity window_ms // tick_ms, default 1800 slots for 30 min at 1 s; non-positive capacity coerced to 1). The ring SHALL pre-allocate capacity Aggregate objects at construction and append SHALL copy the source slot field-by-field over Aggregate.__slots__ into the pre-allocated item at the head, so the ring never stores a reference to the engine's in-flight slot. Append SHALL be O(1) and SHALL overwrite the oldest slot when full (no other eviction); clear() SHALL reset head and size only - it does NOT zero the pre-allocated Aggregate objects, whose stale contents simply become unreachable until the next append overwrites them; snapshot() SHALL return shallow copies (copy.copy) of the live slots in chronological order (oldest first) and an empty list when the ring is empty. cap and size SHALL be exposed as read-only properties.

docs.title: Scenario: Ring overwrite
docs.text:
• WHEN more slots are appended than the ring capacity
  • THEN the oldest slot is overwritten, so the window holds exactly the last capacity slots

docs.title: Scenario: Snapshot isolation
docs.text:
• WHEN a consumer mutates a slot returned by snapshot()
  • THEN the ring's own buffer is unaffected, because each returned slot is a shallow copy

docs.title: Requirement: Canonical 791-key row
docs.text:
The system SHALL emit exactly 791 canonical metric keys per bar plus _bar_close_ts, generated from the fixed layout in keys.py: 33 trade keys, 721 orderbook keys (ob__{5pct|25pct}__{bid|ask}__{11 bases}__{7 suffixes} = 308, ob__cross__{11 d_ bases}__{7 suffixes} = 77, ob__minor__{43 bases}__{7 suffixes} = 301, ob__{bid|ask}__best_size__{7 suffixes} = 14, ob__liq_shock_{bid|ask|mid}__{7 suffixes} = 21), 24 liquidation keys, 12 kline/funding/mark keys, and 1 spread key. Suffixes SHALL be exactly mean, median, sum, q95, min, max, skew. The 11 cone bases SHALL be cost, size, vwap, levels_count, weighted_distance, imbalance, slope, microprice, depth_ratio, log_return_cost, log_return_vwap, and the 11 cross bases the same list prefixed with d_. The key list SHALL be sorted (canonical order matching Go sort.Strings) and its count, uniqueness and sortedness SHALL be asserted at import time against the module constants N_TRADES=33, N_ORDERBOOK=721, N_LIQUIDATIONS=24, N_KLINES_ETC=12, N_SPREAD=1, N_TOTAL=791.

empty_row() SHALL pre-fill all 791 keys with 0.0, so every metric a group cannot compute (empty window, zero denominator, absent data kind) is served as 0.0 - the row never contains NaN, Inf or a missing key. Rows SHALL be produced by compute_all in the fixed order trades -> orderbook -> spread -> liquidations -> klines/funding/mark; each group is a pure function that reads only the ring snapshot, never mutates it, and writes a disjoint subset of the key space, so no group in fact consumes another group's output (the ordering mirrors Go's buildRow sequence; the package docstring's claim that spread and klines depend on compute_orderbook is stale - both read Aggregate fields written by set_book, not row entries, and reordering the calls would not change any value). keys.py SHALL also expose the building blocks by name (SUFFIXES, ORDERBOOK_OFFSETS, ORDERBOOK_SIDES, ORDERBOOK_BASES, ORDERBOOK_CROSS_BASES, ORDERBOOK_MINOR_BASES, TRADE_KEYS, LIQUIDATION_KEYS, KLINE_FUNDING_MARK_KEYS, SPREAD_KEYS), and the orderbook group SHALL import those lists rather than re-declaring them, so the row schema has exactly one source of truth.

docs.title: Scenario: Row schema invariant
docs.text:
• WHEN a row is built
  • THEN it contains exactly 791 metric keys plus _bar_close_ts, every key finite, and the key order is the canonical sorted layout

docs.title: Scenario: Missing data kind
docs.text:
• WHEN a symbol has no funding, no liquidations and no book in the window
  • THEN the corresponding keys are 0.0 rather than NaN or absent

docs.title: Requirement: Suffix statistics
docs.text: The system SHALL derive every suffixed key from seven_stats(xs), which SHALL return mean, median, sum, q95, min, max, skew for a series: min/max from the sorted copy; median linearly interpolated as the mean of the two middle values for even n and the middle value for odd n; q95 as the linearly interpolated 95th percentile over pos = 0.95*(n-1) (the single value when n == 1); sum and mean = sum/n; and skew as Fisher-Pearson g1 m3 / m2**1.5 with m2, m3 the biased central moments, returning 0.0 unless n > 1 and m2 > 0. seven_stats SHALL return all-zero stats for an empty series and SHALL operate on a sorted COPY, never mutating the caller's vector (the same holds for the trade group's _quantile helper). write_suffixed(out, prefix, xs) SHALL write the seven prefix__<suffix> keys, and SHALL write nothing at all for an empty series, leaving those keys at the 0.0 default from empty_row(). write_suffixed SHALL live in the orderbook group module and be re-used by the engine for the liq-shock keys, so all 791 suffixed keys go through one implementation.

docs.title: Scenario: Degenerate series
docs.text:
• WHEN a suffixed series holds a single sample or a constant series
  • THEN skew is 0.0 while mean, median, q95, min and max all equal that value

docs.title: Scenario: Empty series
docs.text:
• WHEN a book-derived series is empty because no slot in the window carried a book
  • THEN write_suffixed writes nothing and all seven keys stay 0.0

docs.title: Requirement: Liquidation shock series
docs.text: The ob__liq_shock_{bid|ask|mid} keys SHALL be the only metric keys written by the engine itself rather than by a group. At each bar the engine SHALL compute the shock series with LiqDeque.rolling_shock(bar_start, bar_close, step_ms=1000, window_ms=10000): a 10-second window stepped in 1-second increments across the whole bar [bar_close_ms - window_ms, bar_close_ms] with BOTH endpoints inclusive (1801 samples for a 30-minute bar at 1-second steps), mapping BUY notional to the bid leg, SELL notional to the ask leg, and their sum to the mid leg, via a two-pointer scan (O(n_steps + n_events)) in which each step sums the events with t - 10000 < ts <= t and sides other than exactly BUY/SELL contribute nothing. The shock notional SHALL be price * resolve_liquidation_size(force) (the same orig_qty -> last_fill_qty -> cum_fill_qty chain as the aggregate path). rolling_shock SHALL return three empty vectors when step_ms <= 0 or bar_close < bar_start; otherwise it always returns non-empty vectors, so the 21 liq-shock keys are written (as zeros) even when no liquidation is in the deque. After the bar the engine SHALL trim the deque with evict_before(bar_close_ms - (window_ms + 10000)).

docs.title: Scenario: Bar with no liquidations
docs.text:
• WHEN a bar closes with an empty liq deque
  • THEN rolling_shock returns three all-zero vectors of 1801 samples and every ob__liq_shock_* key is written as 0.0

docs.title: Scenario: Shock window membership
docs.text:
• WHEN a liquidation lands exactly 10000 ms before a sample point t
  • THEN it has already been evicted from that sample (the window is (t - 10000, t])

docs.title: Requirement: Trade group computations
docs.text: The trade group (33 keys) SHALL accumulate over the ring snapshot: ticks counted for EVERY slot in the window (including slots with no trades, counted before the no-trade skip, so it measures window occupancy in seconds rather than trades); counts, volumes and quote volumes summed over trading slots only; trade_size_max/buy_size_max/sell_size_max as maxima of the per-slot maxima; per-side volume quantiles buy_volume_q50/q95/q99 and their sell mirrors computed over the slots with strictly positive volume on that side; OHLC taken as first-slot open, max of slot highs, min of slot lows, last-slot close; first_ts/last_ts as floats of the first and last trade timestamps. vwap = quote_volume/volume, buy_vwap, sell_vwap SHALL be written only when the matching volume is > 0; herfindahl = sum_square_vol / volume^2 only when volume > 0; kyle_lambda = sum_abs_dp_x_vol / sum_square_vol only when sum_square_vol > 0 (the slot's sum_abs_dp accumulator is not consumed by any group); imbalance = (buy_volume - sell_volume)/(buy_volume + sell_volume) only when that sum is > 0; signed_volume and signed_quote_volume SHALL be written unconditionally. OHLC and first_ts/last_ts SHALL stay 0.0 when the window holds no trade at all. The quantile helper SHALL return 0.0 for an empty series, the minimum for q <= 0, the maximum for q >= 1, and a linear interpolation over the sorted copy otherwise.

docs.title: Scenario: Per-side volume quantiles
docs.text:
• WHEN computing trade metrics
  • THEN buy_volume_q95 is the 95th percentile over slots with positive buy volume only

docs.title: Scenario: Tick count
docs.text:
• WHEN a 30-minute window holds 1800 slots of which only 12 carried trades
  • THEN ticks is 1800, not 12

docs.title: Scenario: Silent window
docs.text:
• WHEN no slot in the window carried a trade
  • THEN open, high, low, close, first_ts, last_ts, vwap, herfindahl and kyle_lambda are all 0.0

docs.title: Requirement: Orderbook group computations
docs.text:
The orderbook group SHALL fill 700 of the 721 orderbook keys (the remaining 21 liq-shock keys come from the engine) and SHALL return immediately on an empty ring snapshot. It SHALL skip every slot without have_book, so all its vectors are indexed by book-bearing slots only. Per book-bearing slot it SHALL derive, for each of the four (offset, side) cones, vwap = cost/size (0.0 when size <= 0), weighted_distance = |vwap - mid|, slope = size/weighted_distance (0.0 when the distance is not > 0), depth_ratio = own size / opposite size (0.0 when the opposite side is not > 0), log_return_cost = log(cost/prev_cost) and log_return_vwap = log(vwap / prev_vwap) where prev_vwap is reconstructed as prev_cost / _safe_one(prev_size) and _safe_one(x) returns 1.0 when x == 0 and x otherwise (so a previous slot with zero size divides by 1 instead of raising). Both log returns SHALL be 0.0 unless the current value and the reconstructed previous value are both strictly positive, which is what makes the first book-bearing slot's log returns 0.0 (the prev_* state starts at 0.0). The per-cone imbalance base SHALL be the slot's imbalance_5pct for both 5% cones and imbalance_25pct for both 25% cones, and the per-cone microprice base SHALL be the same slot microprice for all four cones. ob__bid__best_size and ob__ask__best_size SHALL be fed from the per-slot best_bid_size / best_ask_size.

Cross-snapshot diffs SHALL be computed from the second book-bearing slot onwards (so their vectors are one sample shorter) against the immediately previous book-bearing slot, using the 5% cone: d_cost/d_size on the bid+ask sums, d_vwap and d_slope on the mean of the two side values, d_levels_count and d_weighted_distance on the bid+ask sums, d_imbalance on imbalance_5pct, d_microprice, d_depth_ratio on the bid depth ratio only, and the two d_log_return_* on the same log-return guard.

The 43 minor bases SHALL be: the cumsize ladder (bid_cumsize_5 = bid_5pct_size, bid_cumsize_25 = bid_25pct_size, the extrapolated bid_cumsize_10 = 1.5 * bid_5pct_size and bid_cumsize_50 = 1.25 * bid_25pct_size, plus the ask mirrors); *_cumcost_5/25 from the cone costs; book_curvature_{bid,ask} = (size_25 - size_5)/size_25 (0.0 when size_25 == 0); slope_ratio_{bid,ask} = slope_5/slope_25 (0.0 when the denominator is 0); spread_abs and spread_ticks both equal to the raw spread_abs (no tick size is available); spread_bps = spread/mid*1e4 (0.0 when mid <= 0); midprice and midprice_log_return against the previous book-bearing slot's mid; imbalance_top1 from the best sizes, imbalance_top5 = imbalance_5pct, imbalance_top10 = imbalance_5pct * 0.9, imbalance_top25 = imbalance_25pct; book_age_ms = end_ms - start_ms, i.e. a constant 1000 for every slot; the three book-health counters copied from the slot; levels_total_{bid,ask} from the 25% level counts and levels_above_5pct = ask_25pct_levels - ask_5pct_levels, levels_below_5pct = bid_25pct_levels - bid_5pct_levels; notional_top1_{bid,ask} = best price * best size and notional_top5_{bid,ask} = the 5% cone cost; pressure_{bid,ask} = size_5 * max(0, 1 - weighted_distance/(0.05*mid)) (weight 0.0 when mid <= 0), pressure_signed = bid_5pct_size - ask_5pct_size, pressure_log = log(1 + bid_5pct_size) - log(1 + ask_5pct_size) (0.0 when both sizes are 0); and resilience_{bid,ask} equal to the 5% depth ratios.

docs.title: Scenario: Extrapolated cumulative sizes
docs.text:
• WHEN computing minor orderbook bases
  • THEN bid_cumsize_10 equals 1.5 * bid_5pct_size and bid_cumsize_50 equals 1.25 * bid_25pct_size

docs.title: Scenario: Book-less slots
docs.text:
• WHEN only 30 of the 1800 slots in the window carry a book
  • THEN every orderbook vector holds 30 samples (29 for the cross-diff family) and the suffixed stats are computed over those samples only

docs.title: Scenario: Constant book age
docs.text:
• WHEN ob__minor__book_age_ms__mean is read
  • THEN it is 1000, because the base is the slot duration and not a real staleness measure

docs.title: Requirement: Liquidation, kline, funding, mark and spread group computations
docs.text:
The liquidation group (24 keys) SHALL accumulate each side independently and only from slots whose count on that side is > 0: counts, size sums, notional sums, price sums and average-price sums are summed; liq_*_size_max, liq_*_notional_max and liq_*_price_max are maxima of the per-slot maxima. liq_*_size_mean, liq_*_notional_mean, liq_*_price_mean and liq_*_avg_price_mean SHALL be written only when that side's count is > 0 (per-event means, dividing by the event count, not by the slot count). liq_count, liq_size_sum and liq_notional_sum SHALL be the two-sided totals, and liq_imbalance = (buy_size_sum - sell_size_sum)/(buy_size_sum + sell_size_sum) only when the total is > 0.

The kline/funding/mark group (12 keys) SHALL scan the window once: open_price from the first kline-bearing slot, high_price/low_price as the extremes of the per-slot kline highs/lows, close_price from the last kline-bearing slot, and kline_volume/kline_volume_usd cumulative across kline-bearing slots - all six written only when at least one kline was seen. mark_price, index_price, predicted_funding and next_funding_time_ms SHALL be the latest mark-price observation and are written only when at least one was seen. last_price SHALL be the trade close of the last slot with a trade (a trade field, not the kline close) and realized_funding SHALL be the latest observed funding rate; both are written unconditionally and are 0.0 when never observed.

compute_spread SHALL write the single spread_max key as the maximum spread_abs across book-bearing slots (0.0 when none carries a book).

docs.title: Scenario: Kline bar aggregation
docs.text:
• WHEN computing kline/funding/mark metrics
  • THEN open is the first kline's open, high/low are the extremes, close is the last kline's close, and volume / quote volume are cumulative across slots

docs.title: Scenario: Last price from trades
docs.text:
• WHEN the window carries trades but no klines
  • THEN last_price is the last trade price while close_price stays 0.0

docs.title: Scenario: One-sided liquidations
docs.text:
• WHEN only SELL liquidations occurred in the window
  • THEN every liq_buy_* key is 0.0, the liq_sell_*_mean keys divide by the sell event count, and liq_imbalance is -1.0

docs.title: Requirement: Historical tick reading
docs.text:
The system SHALL read raw ticks from the binance_parser Hive-partitioned parquet layout {data_root}/market={spot|usdm}/type={kind}/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol={SYM}/part-*.parquet via TickReader(data_root, market="usdm"), streaming kind-by-kind while holding at most one parquet file per kind in memory. Exactly five kinds SHALL be read: aggtrades/aggTrades, klines, markprice, funding, booksnapshot; the reader has no converter for forceorder or depth diffs, so a replayed range produces NO FORCE_ORDER tick and every liquidation key and ob__liq_shock_* key in replayed output is 0.0. Day directories SHALL be filtered by overlap at day granularity (day_end < since or day > until is skipped), a dt= directory whose date cannot be parsed SHALL be skipped with a warning, and files SHALL be located by lexicographic path order (relying on dt=YYYY-MM-DD / part-HHMMSS naming) with an extra per-file sort by ts for safety. Kind names aggtrades / aggTrades SHALL be probed as one logical kind and deduplicated through a set[Path] of the globbed paths (plain Path equality, NOT Path.resolve()), which collapses the two spellings on Windows because PureWindowsPath compares case-insensitively; both spellings SHALL then be converted under the first name (aggtrades), since they share a schema. An empty parquet file SHALL be skipped, and _df_to_ticks SHALL return an empty list for any kind it has no converter for. The merged stream (read_ticks_stream) SHALL be a heapq.merge of the per-kind streams keyed on ts, so it is globally ordered by timestamp; read_ticks SHALL materialise the same stream as a list. The per-kind list APIs (read_aggtrades, read_klines, read_markprice, read_funding, read_booksnapshots) SHALL remain available and each SHALL sort its own output by ts; only read_aggtrades goes through the dedup path, the other four glob a single kind directory.

The vectorized converters SHALL map parquet columns to Tick payloads, with Tick.ts taken from timestamp_ms except for klines (open_time) and funding (funding_time_ms), and with optional columns defaulted: side absent -> the is_buyer_maker column, otherwise is_buyer_maker = (side == "sell"); funding mark_price absent or NaN -> 0.0. Book snapshots SHALL be converted row-by-row from the parallel bids_price/bids_size/asks_price/asks_size list columns plus update_id.

docs.title: Scenario: Chronological merge
docs.text:
• WHEN read_ticks_stream consumes all five kinds over a range
  • THEN the emitted Ticks are globally sorted by ts, even when kinds interleave across files

docs.title: Scenario: Case-insensitive kind collision
docs.text:
• WHEN both aggtrades and aggTrades spellings resolve to the same directory on a case-insensitive filesystem
  • THEN the set[Path] dedup collapses them and the reader does not double-read

docs.title: Scenario: No liquidations offline
docs.text:
• WHEN a range is replayed from raw parquet
  • THEN the 24 liquidation keys and the 21 liq-shock keys are all 0.0, because the reader emits no FORCE_ORDER ticks

docs.title: Requirement: Offline replay driver
docs.text:
The system SHALL provide tools/replay_metrics.py as the offline batch driver: run_replay(data_root, output_root, symbols, since, until, market="usdm", window_ms=30*60*1000, tick_ms=1000, book_tick_ms=60_000), with the same defaults exposed on the CLI (--market, --window-ms, --tick-ms, --book-tick-ms) and --from/--to interpreted as inclusive UTC dates (until becomes end-of-day, +1 day - 1 ms). Per symbol it SHALL build one Engine with wall_clock_anchor=False (so bar boundaries follow tick time, never the wall clock) and one BookReplay, hand EVERY streamed tick to book_replay.handle_tick(tick, engine.feed_book) (the replay itself ignores non-snapshots) before engine.push(tick), and then drain emit_if_ready(tick.ts) in a loop so a multi-window gap cannot drop catch-up bars. After the stream ends the driver SHALL drain once bounded by the last tick timestamp and once bounded by the first window boundary after it, so the trailing partial window is emitted exactly once and no zero-filled bars are produced past the data.

Bars SHALL be written as {output_root}/market={market}/type=metrics/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol={SYM}/part-{first_bar_close_ms}.parquet, batched per bar-close day (a single drain may span midnight), zstd-compressed, with columns ts (int64, the bar close), symbol (string) and keys (map<string, double>) holding the 791 metric keys sorted by name with the transport field _bar_close_ts stripped out. Bars SHALL be buffered per symbol and flushed when the TICK day changes (and once more after the final drain), while _flush_bars regroups the buffer by BAR-CLOSE day; the file name SHALL be part-{ts} where ts is the first buffered bar close of that day group, so two flushes touching the same day produce two files unless their first bar close collides. The driver SHALL print per-day progress, and SHALL exit with status 1 and an ERROR line when zero bars were written across all symbols.

docs.title: Scenario: Trailing partial window
docs.text:
• WHEN the last tick of a range lands mid-window
  • THEN the driver drains to the first boundary after that tick so the final bar is emitted, and stops there instead of draining to wall-clock now

docs.title: Scenario: Persisted schema
docs.text:
• WHEN a metrics parquet file is written
  • THEN it has ts, symbol and a sorted keys map of 791 float64 entries, and _bar_close_ts appears only as the ts column

docs.title: Requirement: Live metrics bridge
docs.text:
The system SHALL deliver live metrics in-process via LiveMetricsBridge(symbols, market="usdm", lookback_days=30, window_ms=30*60*1000, tick_ms=1000, book_tick_ms=60_000): one Engine per symbol (all wall_clock_anchor=True), subscribed to binance_parser's live tick stream, with ticks for symbols outside the constructor list dropped. The two ingestion paths (on_tick for direct tick pushes and consume_bus for the async bus consumer) SHALL be mutually exclusive - a tick pushed while the bus consumer is active SHALL be error-logged and dropped, and a second consume_bus SHALL raise RuntimeError; the active flag SHALL be released in a finally block so a WS reconnect can re-subscribe. consume_bus SHALL convert events with the adapter, skip unconvertible events and unknown symbols, feed SNAPSHOT events through a per-symbol BookReplay (whose callback binds the symbol eagerly and routes to on_book_scalars, which caches the latest scalars per symbol and calls Engine.feed_book) and then push the same tick into the engine, and drain rows via emit_if_ready into a per-symbol deque. Both paths SHALL build rows OUTSIDE the bar lock and take the lock only to publish finished bars; the engines themselves are single-threaded per symbol.

Bars SHALL be stored as (bar_close_ms, row) pairs and evicted when older than lookback_days (default 30) measured from the WALL CLOCK at store time, and eviction only runs when new bars arrive. exchange_data(until_ts, lookback_days=None) SHALL serve a rolling window as a dict-like metrics container over a UTC pd.date_range(since, until_ts) index whose frequency is window_ms // 60000 minutes (30min by default), exposed under BOTH the binance and binance-f exchange keys as the SAME container object. A lookback_days argument of 0 SHALL fall back to the constructor default (the code uses lookback_days or self.lookback_days). Frames SHALL be built per metric by scanning bars in [since_ms, until_ts_ms], dropping NaN values, keeping the last bar per timestamp, and reindexing to the served index (missing timestamps become NaN); a symbol with no in-window value for that key SHALL get an all-NaN column of the served index; price-like frames SHALL then have 0.0 replaced by NaN and be forward-filled; per-key frames SHALL be cached under the REQUESTED name (so zero frames and the funding frame are cached too). latest_metric_ts SHALL return the newest bar close across symbols as a UTC timestamp, or None.

The bridge SHALL also expose the GoExchangeData-compatible introspection surface the trader relies on: has_key(go_key), which is True only when some bar in the served window holds a value that is present, non-zero AND non-NaN (so a genuinely zero metric reads as absent) and which probes RAW row keys without passing them through go_name; has_kinds/missing_kinds for kind-gating against the _KIND_PROBES table - trades -> (vwap, buy_volume_q95), klines -> (close, quote_volume), markprice -> (close,), orderbook -> (ob__25pct__bid__cost__mean,), go_metrics -> (ob__minor__spread_bps__mean, vwap) - where ALL probes of a kind must pass, an unknown kind name is always reported missing, and the exchange argument is accepted but ignored; __contains__, which is False only for zero-served metrics; and get, which returns its default only on KeyError (in practice unreachable, because go_name passes unknown names through and __getitem__ then serves an all-NaN frame).

warm_start_from_parquet(root) SHALL load {root}/market={market}/type=metrics/symbol={SYM}/*.parquet (columns ts and keys only, 8 worker threads), keep only rows with ts >= now - lookback_days, re-add _bar_close_ts to each row, sort per symbol, and replace that symbol's deque wholesale - a symbol that loaded no row keeps whatever deque it already had. The glob SHALL have NO dt= partition level, so it matches a flat type=metrics/symbol=<SYM>/ layout and does NOT match the type=metrics/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/symbol=<SYM>/ layout written by tools/replay_metrics.py; a warm start pointed at replay output therefore loads 0 bars and only logs the zero-bar warning. It SHALL skip unreadable files with a warning, raise FileNotFoundError only when the type=metrics directory is missing, log a warning when the total is 0, and return the number of bars loaded.

docs.title: Scenario: Ingestion mutual exclusion
docs.text:
• WHEN a tick arrives through on_tick while consume_bus is active
  • THEN the tick is logged as an error and dropped, so engines are never double-fed

docs.title: Scenario: Rolling window eviction
docs.text:
• WHEN a finished bar is older than lookback_days relative to the current wall clock
  • THEN it is removed from the served deque on the next store

docs.title: Scenario: Zero reads as absent
docs.text:
• WHEN every bar in the window carries ob__25pct__bid__cost__mean = 0.0
  • THEN has_key reports False and missing_kinds reports orderbook as missing

docs.title: Scenario: Warm start replaces deque
docs.text:
• WHEN warm_start_from_parquet loads at least one bar for a symbol
  • THEN the loaded bars replace that symbol's deque entirely rather than merging with live bars

docs.title: Scenario: Warm start against replay output
docs.text:
• WHEN warm_start_from_parquet is pointed at a root written by tools/replay_metrics.py
  • THEN the symbol={SYM}/*.parquet glob finds nothing under the dt=-partitioned layout, 0 bars are returned and a warning is logged instead of an exception

docs.title: Requirement: Metric-name resolution
docs.text:
The system SHALL resolve backtest metric names to live 791-key names through keys.go_name(metric, market="spot"), which returns (go_key, price_like): predicted_funding is the only name in _ZERO_METRICS and SHALL resolve to (None, False) so the bridge serves a zero frame; price-like aliases (close_price -> close, open_price -> open, high_price -> high, low_price -> low, last_price, vwap) SHALL return price_like=True; mark_price/index_price SHALL alias to close ONLY on spot, and SHALL pass through unchanged (still price-like) on any other market, because derivatives carry a genuine mark and index price. Flow aliases SHALL map volume -> volume (an explicit identity entry that classifies volume as NOT price-like, so it is never zero-to-NaN forward-filled), volume_usd -> quote_volume, buy_cost -> buy_quote_volume, sell_cost -> sell_quote_volume, and every {buy,sell}_cost_0.XX, {buy,sell}_cost_quantile_0.XX and {buy,sell}_volume_quantile_0.XX_usd spelling onto {buy,sell}_volume_q{50,95,99}. Orderbook names matching ^(bid|ask)_(\d+)_(cost|vwap|size|slope|imbalance|depth_ratio|levels_count|microprice)_(avg|mean|median|min|max|sum|q95|skew)$ SHALL map to ob__{pct}pct__{side}__{feat}__{stat} with the backtest stat avg aliased to mean, and SHALL be price-like only for vwap and microprice. Resolution order SHALL be zero-metrics -> price-like aliases -> flow aliases -> orderbook regex -> pass-through. Any other name SHALL pass through unchanged (never raising, despite the docstring's KeyError claim) so callers can request a raw Backend-go key directly; in the live bridge an unmapped name therefore resolves to an all-NaN frame rather than an error.

realized_funding SHALL be served with settlement semantics: the underlying stream repeats the accruing 8h rate in every bar, so the bridge SHALL zero the frame everywhere except rows at minute 0 of the hours in FUNDING_SETTLEMENT_HOURS ({0, 8, 16}), where it charges the PRIOR bar's rate (a one-row shift, NaN filled with 0.0).

docs.title: Scenario: Funding settlement hours
docs.text:
• WHEN a realized_funding series is served
  • THEN the rate is charged only on rows at minute 0 of hours 0, 8, and 16 (the prior bar's rate), and is zero elsewhere

docs.title: Scenario: Derivatives mark price
docs.text:
• WHEN mark_price is requested with market="usdm"
  • THEN it resolves to the real mark_price key instead of the kline close proxy used on spot

docs.title: Scenario: Unmapped name
docs.text:
• WHEN a strategy asks for a name no alias covers
  • THEN go_name returns it unchanged and the live container serves an all-NaN frame instead of raising

docs.title: Requirement: Offline metrics container divergence
docs.text: The offline container (AggregatedMetricsDict / ExchangeData in alpha_engine/metrics/metrics_dict.py) SHALL diverge deliberately from the live bridge. Unknown metric names SHALL raise KeyError from _resolve_source (never resolving to NaN frames - the opposite of the live bridge's pass-through), and a name that resolves to a group whose aggregator did not produce it SHALL also raise KeyError. Group aggregation SHALL be lazy and cached: the first access of any metric in a group aggregates that group for ALL tickers over a 30min UTC index, and tickers with no data for a metric SHALL be filled with an all-NaN column. When NO ticker in a group produced data, the group SHALL still be marked aggregated and nothing written, so the pending lookup falls through to the "aggregator did not produce it" KeyError rather than looping. When the caller passes no explicit ticker list, the ticker set SHALL be the sorted union of the reader's available_tickers for the trades and klines kinds only. ExchangeData SHALL default to the exchanges ["binance", "binance-f"], one AggregatedMetricsDict each. has_kinds/missing_kinds SHALL gate against the underlying reader's available_tickers per kind - fully permissive (always True / empty set) when no reader is attached (mock mode), and treating a reader exception as a missing kind - a different mechanism from the live bridge's _KIND_PROBES table.

docs.title: Scenario: Unknown metric is fatal offline
docs.text:
• WHEN a strategy asks the offline container for a name no aggregator registers
  • THEN a KeyError is raised instead of a NaN frame, so the typo surfaces in the backtest

docs.title: Scenario: Mock mode gating
docs.text:
• WHEN has_kinds is called on a container with no reader attached
  • THEN it returns True for every kind, because there is nothing to probe

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines the typed data contracts of binance_parser: market abstraction, live WebSocket DTOs, historical row schemas, REST response DTOs, and the shared rate limiter that all Binance-facing callers rely on.

docs.title: Requirement: Market abstraction
docs.text: The system SHALL model a market as one of exactly two values: spot or usdm (USD-M perpetual futures). All venue-specific URLs (WebSocket base, REST base, exchange-info path, depth-snapshot path, history base) SHALL be defined per market in single configuration maps. CLI parsing of a market argument SHALL accept spot, usdm, or both (expands to both markets); any other value SHALL be rejected with an error.

docs.title: Scenario: CLI market parsing
docs.text:
• WHEN the market argument is both
  • THEN the system resolves it to the ordered list ["spot", "usdm"]

docs.title: Scenario: Invalid market value
docs.text:
• WHEN the market argument is not spot, usdm, or both
  • THEN the system raises a ValueError naming the offending value

docs.title: Scenario: Adding a new market
docs.text:
• WHEN a new market value is introduced
  • THEN it requires a corresponding entry in the five venue-specific configuration maps (WebSocket base, REST base, exchange-info path, depth-snapshot path, history base), plus per-market entries in the depth snapshot max-limit and bootstrap-stagger maps (indexed by market at bootstrap time); other REST endpoints (funding, market-stats, margin interest) remain fixed constants outside the maps

docs.title: Requirement: Live WebSocket DTOs
docs.text: The system SHALL deserialize every subscribed Binance stream event into a typed DTO with a fixed pyarrow schema. Every DTO SHALL expose its schema, an event_type identifier, and a row serializer for parquet persistence. All timestamps SHALL be int64 milliseconds; wire-derived timestamps are UTC, and a depth event without a wire timestamp falls back to the local clock, while a mark-price event prefers the event time E over T. Price and quantity columns SHALL be float32, except mark-price fields which SHALL be float64.

docs.title: Scenario: Depth diff DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a @depth payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes an orderbook event carrying symbol, event timestamp, first/last/previous update ids, and parallel bid/ask price and size lists, and is dispatched to the in-memory book only - never persisted as a row

docs.title: Scenario: Depth diff market difference
docs.text:
• WHEN a @depth payload arrives on spot
  • THEN the previous-update id is always null (spot diffs carry no pu), while usdm diffs carry it

docs.title: Scenario: Trade DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a @trade payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes a trades event with trade id, timestamp, price, quantity, and side (buy when the payload's m flag is falsy, else sell)

docs.title: Scenario: AggTrade DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN an @aggTrade payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes an aggtrades event with aggregate trade id, first/last constituent trade ids, timestamp, price, quantity, and side

docs.title: Scenario: Mark price DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a @markPrice@1s payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes a markprice event with mark price, index price, predicted funding rate (all float64), and next funding time

docs.title: Scenario: Liquidation DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a @forceOrder payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes a forceorder event whose fields are read from the nested o object, with the side mapped from uppercase BUY/other to buy/sell

docs.title: Scenario: Kline DTO
docs.text:
• WHEN a closed @kline_<interval> payload is parsed
  • THEN it becomes a klines event with open/close times, OHLCV, quote volume, taker-buy volumes, trade count (int32), and closed flag

docs.title: Requirement: Stream event dispatch
docs.text: The system SHALL map a raw stream message to its DTO by substring matching on the stream name, in a fixed precedence order: @depth, then @markPrice, then @aggTrade, then @forceOrder, then @trade, then @kline. Messages whose stream matches none of these SHALL be rejected as unknown (the rejection is a ValueError subclass); a @kline payload whose bar is not yet closed SHALL also be rejected as unknown (running bars are dropped).

docs.title: Scenario: Dispatch precedence of force order over trade
docs.text:
• WHEN a stream name contains both @forceOrder and @trade
  • THEN the payload is parsed as a forceorder event, not a trades event

docs.title: Scenario: Running kline rejection
docs.text:
• WHEN a @kline payload has its x (closed) flag false
  • THEN the system rejects the message as an unknown running-kline stream and it is not persisted

docs.title: Requirement: Historical row schemas
docs.text: The system SHALL define pyarrow schemas for historical archive rows: klines (11 columns, trades int32), aggTrades, trades, bookTicker, and funding rate. These schemas SHALL be available in a registry keyed by archive data type, and SHALL map to pandas read dtypes for CSV ingestion. All timestamps SHALL be int64 milliseconds UTC; prices and quantities float32.

docs.title: Scenario: Schema registry coverage
docs.text:
• WHEN a historical data type is klines, aggTrades, trades, bookTicker, or funding
  • THEN a schema exists for it in the registry

docs.title: Scenario: CSV dtype mapping
docs.text:
• WHEN pandas dtypes are derived from a schema for CSV reading
  • THEN bool columns are excluded from the mapping so they are not coerced to object strings during read

docs.title: Requirement: Funding rate row
docs.text: The system SHALL parse REST funding-rate records into a funding row with symbol, funding time (ms), funding rate (float32), and optional mark price (float32, null when absent). The symbol, funding time, and funding rate are required keys in the source payload (accessed with [], so a missing one raises KeyError); only mark price is optional via .get().

docs.title: Scenario: Funding row with mark price
docs.text:
• WHEN a REST record contains fundingTime, fundingRate, and markPrice
  • THEN the parsed row carries all four fields and serializes to a single row dict

docs.title: Scenario: Funding row without mark price
docs.text:
• WHEN a REST record omits markPrice
  • THEN the parsed row has a null mark price and still serializes successfully

docs.title: Requirement: REST exchange metadata DTOs
docs.text: The system SHALL parse exchange-info payloads into a per-symbol row with symbol, status, contract type, tick size (from PRICE_FILTER), step size (from LOT_SIZE), min notional (from MIN_NOTIONAL, falling back to NOTIONAL variants), max leverage (maximum initialLeverage across leverage brackets), maintenance margin rate (of the lowest bracket), default maker/taker fees, and the full leverage-bracket curve. Missing filters SHALL become NaN; missing brackets SHALL yield zero max leverage, NaN maintenance margin rate, and an empty bracket list. Exchange-info payloads SHALL also be parsed into a simpler ExchangeInfoSymbol DTO (symbol, status, base asset, quote asset, optional contract type - empty for spot) with is_trading and is_perpetual convenience properties, used for the non-persisted exchangeInfo shape.

docs.title: Scenario: Spot vs USD-M notional shape
docs.text:
• WHEN the source payload exposes min notional only through the NOTIONAL filter
  • THEN the system falls back to that filter's minNotional and then notional field

docs.title: Scenario: No leverage brackets
docs.text:
• WHEN a symbol has no leverage-bracket data
  • THEN its row has max leverage 0, maintenance margin rate NaN, and an empty bracket list

docs.title: Requirement: Market-stats REST rows
docs.text: The system SHALL parse five distinct market-statistics responses into rows with namespaced columns and float64 numeric fields: open interest now, global long/short account ratio, top long/short account ratio, top long/short position ratio, and spot margin daily interest rate. Ratio and quantity strings in responses SHALL be cast to float; column names SHALL be namespaced by the source endpoint so identical concepts from different endpoints do not collide; event types SHALL be distinct from the legacy periodic-metrics event types.

docs.title: Scenario: Symbol absent from ratio payloads
docs.text:
• WHEN the global/top long-short payloads do not carry the symbol
  • THEN the caller injects the symbol into the row during parsing

docs.title: Scenario: Hourly to daily interest rescale
docs.text:
• WHEN a spot margin payload provides the next hourly interest rate
  • THEN the parsed row stores the rate multiplied by 24 as a daily rate

docs.title: Requirement: Legacy periodic futures metrics
docs.text: The system SHALL parse three /futures/data/ responses (open-interest history, taker long/short ratio, top long/short position ratio) into rows that keep numeric values as strings, with all columns non-nullable: open_interest, taker_ratio, and long_short_ratio events. These SHALL use event types distinct from the market-stats rows and SHALL persist sum_open_interest, sum_open_interest_value, buy_sell_ratio, buy_vol, sell_vol, long_short_ratio, long_account, and short_account as string columns.

docs.title: Scenario: Taker ratio symbol injection
docs.text:
• WHEN a taker-ratio payload omits the symbol (Binance does not include it)
  • THEN the fetch helper injects the symbol into the row before parsing

docs.title: Scenario: Numeric strings preserved
docs.text:
• WHEN a /futures/data/ response contains a numeric value
  • THEN the row keeps it as its original string representation, never casting to float

docs.title: Requirement: Rate limiter
docs.text: The system SHALL throttle Binance REST requests with token-bucket limiters. A multi-bucket limiter SHALL route each request to the first bucket whose pattern is a substring of the request URL, with an empty-string pattern as the catch-all default; an empty bucket list SHALL be rejected at construction, and a request matching no bucket at all SHALL trip an internal assertion. The canonical USD-M limiter SHALL provide a /futures/data/ bucket of 400 weight per 300 seconds and a default bucket of 2000 weight per 60 seconds. A request costing more than a bucket's capacity SHALL be rejected with an error.

docs.title: Scenario: URL-to-bucket routing
docs.text:
• WHEN a request URL contains /futures/data/
  • THEN it is charged to the 400-weight/300-second bucket, and all other URLs to the 2000-weight/60-second bucket

docs.title: Scenario: Bucket exhaustion waits
docs.text:
• WHEN a bucket lacks tokens for a request
  • THEN the limiter sleeps until enough tokens refill before releasing the request

docs.title: Scenario: Over-capacity cost
docs.text:
• WHEN a request costs more than the target bucket's capacity
  • THEN the limiter raises an error rather than waiting

docs.title: Requirement: Rate-limit error semantics
docs.text: The system SHALL treat HTTP 429 (rate limited) and 418 (IP banned) as rate-limit responses: parse Retry-After from headers (falling back to 60 seconds), and cap consecutive rate-limit waits per REST call at 3.

docs.title: Scenario: Retry-After parsing
docs.text:
• WHEN a rate-limit response carries a Retry-After header
  • THEN the system uses that value as the wait duration, defaulting to 60 seconds when absent or malformed

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines the REST polling pipelines of binance_parser that run alongside the live WebSocket listener: funding-rate polling aligned to exchange settlements, the daily exchange-metadata poll, futures market-stats polling, the optional signed spot margin-interest poll, and the periodic-metrics pollers. It pins the polling cadences, the shared retry and rate-limit policy, and the parquet types each poller writes.

docs.title: Requirement: Poller session and retry policy
docs.text: All REST pollers SHALL follow one retry policy: transient errors (network, 5xx) SHALL back off over (1, 3, 10) seconds, and 429/418 rate-limit responses SHALL be honored by sleeping per Retry-After, up to 3 waits per call. Non-retryable 4xx (any 4xx other than 408/429/500/502/503/504) SHALL cause the current cycle to be skipped (return None), without retries; the notification medium differs by poller - funding and exchange-info pollers print(...) to stdout, while market-stats and periodic pollers use log.warning (nothing printed). Each poller SHALL open its own HTTP session (no shared session object); the endpoint weight of every USD-M call SHALL be acquired from the shared multi-bucket rate limiter before the request, and the USD-M limiter SHALL be shared by all USD-M pollers and the depth bootstrap. The spot-margin poller passes no limiter and relies on its own hourly alignment.

docs.title: Scenario: Connect-error backoff
docs.text:
• WHEN a poll fails with a connection error
  • THEN it is retried after 1, then 3, then 10 seconds, then the cycle is skipped

docs.title: Scenario: Rate-limit wait
docs.text:
• WHEN a poll returns 429 with a Retry-After header
  • THEN the client sleeps for the announced duration (up to 3 waits per call) and then retries

docs.title: Scenario: Non-retryable 4xx
docs.text:
• WHEN a poll returns 403
  • THEN it is printed as a permanent failure and the cycle is skipped without retry

docs.title: Requirement: Funding-rate poller
docs.text: The system SHALL poll the USD-M funding-rate endpoint (/fapi/v1/fundingRate, weight 1) once per symbol per cycle with limit=1, for the configured symbol set, and persist rows under type=funding (market usdm) with a single flush() per cycle (one partition per day/symbol instead of one file per row). The first cycle SHALL run immediately; later cycles SHALL sleep until the next UTC settlement hour (00/08/16) plus 30 seconds (minimum 1 second). Requests SHALL be bounded by the configured funding parallelism (5); an empty response SHALL yield no row.

docs.title: Scenario: Settlement-aligned poll
docs.text:
• WHEN the funding poller finishes a cycle at 05:00 UTC
  • THEN it sleeps until 08:00 UTC plus 30 seconds, then polls again

docs.title: Scenario: Empty funding response
docs.text:
• WHEN the endpoint returns no rows for a symbol
  • THEN no row is written for that symbol for the cycle

docs.title: Requirement: Exchange-info poller
docs.text: The system SHALL poll the USD-M exchange metadata once per UTC day: the first cycle SHALL run immediately, later cycles SHALL run daily at 00:05 UTC. Each cycle SHALL fetch exchangeInfo (weight 10) and leverageBracket (weight 1) in parallel and build one row per symbol by cross-joining the two payloads (filtered to the configured symbols), persisted under type=exchange_info (market usdm). Each persisted row SHALL carry maker_fee / taker_fee defaulted to the USD-M VIP-0 schedule (0.0002 / 0.0005) rather than real account fees. The poller SHALL run only when USD-M is part of the live run. When MIN_QUOTE_VOLUME_24H_USD is set, the cycle SHALL additionally fetch the full-market 24-hour ticker batch (weight 40) and drop symbols whose 24h quote volume is below the threshold; a failed volume fetch SHALL skip the filter entirely (symbols are not silently lost), unparsable quote volumes SHALL count as 0 with a warning, and non-finite values SHALL count as 0 silently.

docs.title: Scenario: Daily schedule with immediate first cycle
docs.text:
• WHEN the live run starts at 12:00 UTC
  • THEN the exchange-info cycle runs immediately, then every day at 00:05 UTC

docs.title: Scenario: Empty payload body
docs.text:
• WHEN the exchange-info endpoint returns HTTP 200 with an error body that has no symbols (e.g. Binance code -1003)
  • THEN the cycle is skipped with a printed message

docs.title: Scenario: Missing leverage brackets
docs.text:
• WHEN the leverageBracket payload is not a list
  • THEN the cycle continues with empty brackets: max_leverage persists as 0 (the schema is int32 and cannot hold NaN), while maintenance_margin_rate persists as NaN

docs.title: Scenario: Volume filter
docs.text:
• WHEN MIN_QUOTE_VOLUME_24H_USD is set and the 24h ticker fetch succeeds
  • THEN symbols below the quote-volume threshold are dropped from the persisted rows

docs.title: Requirement: Market-stats poller (futures)
docs.text: The system SHALL poll, for the configured symbol set, four endpoints per symbol in parallel: open interest (/fapi/v1/openInterest, rows open_interest_now), global long/short account ratio, top long/short account ratio, and top long/short position ratio (rows global_long_accounts, top_long_accounts, top_long_positions). Cycles SHALL align to 5-minute UTC slots (always the next slot, so the same bucket is never polled twice), with the first cycle immediately; a slow cycle that crosses a slot boundary SHALL skip that slot rather than queue up. Requests SHALL be bounded by the market-stats parallelism (5). For ratio endpoints Binance returns arrays oldest-first, so only the LAST element SHALL be used; an empty array SHALL yield no row. A row SHALL be written only when the result is not None, and an open-interest parse error (missing key or wrong type) SHALL log a warning and skip that row without stopping the cycle.

docs.title: Scenario: Five-minute slot alignment
docs.text:
• WHEN the market-stats poller starts mid-slot
  • THEN the first cycle fires immediately, and from the second cycle on the polls are issued at the next 5-minute UTC boundary

docs.title: Scenario: Last-array-element ratio
docs.text:
• WHEN a ratio endpoint returns a non-empty array
  • THEN only the last (latest) element is persisted

docs.title: Scenario: Parse error survival
docs.text:
• WHEN an open-interest row cannot be parsed
  • THEN the row is skipped with a warning and the cycle continues

docs.title: Requirement: Market-stats spot interest poller
docs.text: The system SHALL optionally poll the signed margin interest endpoint (/sapi/v1/margin/next-hourly-interest-rate, per the configured margin-interest URL) with hourly UTC alignment, persisting rows under type=daily_interest_rate (market spot). The poller SHALL run only when the margin-interest flag is enabled AND spot is part of the live run, with the asset list taken from the configured MARGIN_INTEREST_ASSETS. The request SHALL be signed (HMAC-SHA256 over the query with the margin API secret, signature in the query string, API key in the X-MBX-APIKEY header). The poller SHALL refuse to start when the feature flag is disabled (info log), when the API key/secret are empty (one warning), or when there are no assets, no symbols, or no matches (info log and exit). The endpoint returns a per-hour rate; the stored value SHALL be that hourly rate multiplied by 24 (daily-equivalent daily_interest_rate = hourly x 24). Each interest rate SHALL be duplicated onto every symbol that matches its asset (symbol.startswith(asset) and symbol != asset).

docs.title: Scenario: Disabled margin poller
docs.text:
• WHEN the margin-interest flag is disabled
  • THEN the poller logs an info message and does not start

docs.title: Scenario: Asset-to-symbol matching
docs.text:
• WHEN an asset matches several symbols
  • THEN the same interest rate is written for each matching symbol

docs.title: Requirement: Periodic-metrics pollers
docs.text: The system SHALL provide a generic periodic poller over three USD-M metric kinds: open-interest history, taker long/short ratio, and top long/short position ratio (type={kind}). Each poller SHALL be constructed per (kind, symbol) with a polling interval (default 300 seconds), a Binance period parameter (default 5m), and a limit of 2 candles (the latest and the previous one), and SHALL run an endless loop sleeping interval between cycles. An unknown kind SHALL raise ValueError listing the valid kinds. Rate-limit exhaustion inside a cycle SHALL produce an empty cycle (no rows, no crash); any unexpected exception SHALL be logged with log.exception and re-raised (escalation instead of silent continuation). The pollers SHALL run only when the periodic-poller flag is enabled and USD-M is part of the live run.

docs.title: Scenario: Unknown kind rejected
docs.text:
• WHEN a poller is constructed with a kind outside the three supported ones
  • THEN it raises ValueError naming the valid kinds

docs.title: Scenario: Rate-limit exhaustion
docs.text:
• WHEN a cycle exhausts the rate-limit retry budget
  • THEN the cycle produces no rows and the loop continues without crashing

docs.title: Scenario: Unexpected error escalation
docs.text:
• WHEN a cycle hits an unexpected exception
  • THEN it is logged with log.exception and re-raised rather than silently swallowed

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
Lookup material — flat lists, tables, glossary entries.

Page What it lists CLI Every flag of python main.py (root) and python binance_parser/main.py Operators All ops in alpha_engine/operators.py with signatures and edge cases Metrics catalogue Every metric name data["…"]["…"] accepts, by group Glossary Domain terms — alpha, Sharpe, drawdown, funding, …

If you're looking for narrative documentation (how the pipeline works, how to write a strategy, how to deploy), see the Alpha engine or Binance parser sections.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text: Entry points — root main.py (live trader), tools/ (offline tools) and binance_parser/main.py (data pipeline).

docs.title: Root — alpha engine (live trader only)
docs.text:
python main.py [-h] {live-trade}

If no subcommand is given (python main.py, python main.py --market usdm), defaults to live-trade.

docs.title: live-trade
docs.text:
The live trader takes no CLI flags — it is configured entirely by live_config.yaml at the repo root. Edit that file (strategy, universe, bar cadence, mode, risk caps, paths, ...), then run:

python main.py live-trade      # or: python main.py live   (Docker entrypoint alias)

Every parameter lives in the YAML; env is reserved for BINANCE_* secrets. A missing file, a missing required key, or an unparseable/invalid value fails loud. To run a different profile, edit the single repo-root live_config.yaml or bind-mount a different file over /app/live_config.yaml in Docker. See the annotated live_config.yaml for the full key list and defaults.

Full description: Live trading.

docs.title: Backtest — tool
docs.text:
Moved out of main.py; the offline backtest runs as a tool:

python tools/backtest.py [-h]
    [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD]
    [--alphas {ob_mispricing,vol_ob_entropy,funding_reversion,
               trade_imbalance,vol_mean_reversion,book_depth_imbalance} ...]
    [--data-root DATA_ROOT] [--mock] [--metrics-roots ROOTS …]
    [--tickers SYM …] [--execution {close,vwap}]
    [--max-w F] [--fee-bps F] [--slippage-bps F] [--spread-default-bps F]
    [--combine {markowitz,risk_parity,ew}]
    [--max-strategy-weight F] [--alloc-lookback-days N]
    [--no-plot] [--log-level LEVEL]
Flag Default Meaning --since 2023-06-01 UTC start date. --until 2024-06-01 UTC end date. --alphas funding_reversion One or more strategy keys. --data-root data Parquet root in the parser's Hive layout. --mock off Use MockRawDataReader (synthetic data, no I/O). --metrics-roots — Precomputed metrics roots (bypass raw aggregation). --execution vwap vwap (next-bar VWAP fill) or close (instant, legacy). --no-plot off Skip the matplotlib dashboard.

Examples:

# Synthetic 1-week run, no plot
python tools/backtest.py --mock --since 2024-01-01 --until 2024-01-08 \
    --alphas funding_reversion --no-plot

# Real-data Q1 2025 with two strategies
python tools/backtest.py --since 2025-01-01 --until 2025-04-01 \
    --alphas funding_reversion trade_imbalance --data-root data

See tools/README.md for the full flag reference.
